articles.title: El Arsenal va a por todo
articles.standfirst: Para 777 es el favorito a ganar la EFL Cup
articles.summary: Para 777 es el favorito a ganar la EFL Cup
articles.body: La Carabao Cup entra en su fase de definiciones. Entre el 27 y el 29 de octubre se juegan los octavos de final, con cruces que dejan un torneo muy cargado de nombres propios y con las eliminatorias a partido único como gran fuente de sorpresas. En ese escenario, el mercado de casas de apuestas tiene un claro favorito para levantar el trofeo en Wembley. El Arsenal es ese candidato, con una cuota de 3.25 en 777. Los de Arteta llegan como campeones de la última Premier League, pero su recuerdo más reciente en esta competición es una final perdida: cayeron 2-0 ante el Manchester City, con doblete de Nico O’Reilly. El sorteo les ha sido favorable, porque visitan hoy al Fleetwood Town, el equipo peor clasificado de los que quedan, en un cruce asequible justo cuando más rotación necesita su plantilla. Ese camino despejado explica en buena parte que el mercado le coloque en cabeza. Por detrás aparece el Manchester City en las apuestas deportivas, a cuota 4.5, que es precisamente el actual campeón y el club que ha convertido este torneo en una de sus especialidades. Suma nueve títulos, siete de ellos desde 2014, y con Guardiola encadenó cuatro seguidos entre 2018 y 2021. La temporada pasada eliminó al Newcastle en semifinales con un global de 5-1 antes de superar al Arsenal en la final. Este miércoles recibe al Brighton en los octavos, y su cuota premia esa experiencia, aunque también refleja que en la Premier el título se le escapó ante los gunners. La parte más atractiva del cuadro llega con el duelo de mañana en Anfield, donde el Liverpool recibe al Chelsea y un grande se quedará fuera antes de los cuartos. Los Reds, a cuota 7, son el club más laureado de la historia de la competición, con diez títulos, y la ganaron en 2024 al vencer precisamente a los blues en la final. Llegan con cuatro victorias seguidas y el factor campo a favor, aunque la final perdida de 2025 ante el Newcastle recuerda que su dominio no es incontestable. El Chelsea, a cuota 7.5, parte un escalón por debajo en el mercado por su irregularidad reciente y por las dudas que rodean su portería, pero tiene argumentos para hacer daño. Fue semifinalista el curso pasado y perdió aquella final de 2024, por lo que conoce bien las rondas decisivas. Su precio es el de un equipo con plantilla para competir con cualquiera, aunque obligado a ganar en un campo en el que los visitantes sufren. Más lejos en el mercado aparece el Newcastle, a cuota 17, campeón de esta competición en 2025 tras vencer al Liverpool en Wembley y semifinalista la temporada pasada. Visita al Everton el jueves en un partido que puede dar mucho valor a quien confíe en su experiencia reciente. Es un equipo que sabe lo que cuesta ganar este torneo, algo que no todos los que cotizan por delante pueden decir. El Aston Villa cierra el grupo de aspirantes, también a 17. El conjunto de Birmingham se mide al Bournemouth y tiene calidad individual suficiente para competir con cualquiera, aunque no cuenta con la tradición copera de los candidatos de arriba. Su cuota es la de un equipo capaz de dar la sorpresa, pero al que le falta el pedigrí de los que han levantado el trofeo en los últimos años.

articles.title: European Curling Championships 2026: Scotland men & women win opening two ties
articles.summary: Scotland men and women both have two wins out of two at the European Curling Championships in Ostrava in the Czech Republic.
articles.body:
Scotland men and women both have two wins out of two at the European Curling Championships in Ostrava in the Czech Republic.

Fay Henderson's rink defeated Turkey 7-4 on Wednesday after a comprehensive 12-3 victory over Denmark on Tuesday.

Against Turkey, Scotland women were two up after the first end but trailed by the the end of the third before picking up a three. Turkey got back within one after the sixth but a two at the next end got the Scots over the line.

In the opener, they edged the opening two ends by single points before the Danes halved the deficit. However, the Scots took control, surging into a five-point lead by the close of the fourth end.

Although Denmark scored two points in the fifth, Scotland ended the contest emphatically with a six-point haul in the sixth and final end.

Both of Scotland men's opening ties took place on Wednesday - an 8-4 win over the Netherlands and a 9-2 victory against Belgium.

Grant Hardie's rink picked up two at the opening end and three at the third to lead the Dutch 5-1. It was 6-4 after six ends but Scotland picked up two more at the seventh to see out the win.

Scotland men were 7-0 up after two ends against the Belgians, who picked up a single at the third and another at the fifth for 8-2 but a final single at the sixth completed the Scots' win.

Scotland women face Sweden on Thursday (08:30 GMT), with the round-robin match live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.

Scotland men meet Germany on Thursday afternoon.

articles.title: FBI reportedly advised Pat McAfee to wear bulletproof vest following Charlie Kirk killing
articles.summary: During a bizarre rant on his show Monday about his bad experience co-hosting College GameDay from the University of Utah, ESPN star Pat McAfee made reference...
articles.body:
During a bizarre rant on his show Monday about his bad experience co-hosting College GameDay from the University of Utah, ESPN star Pat McAfee made reference to the killing of Charlie Kirk last year.

The rant stemmed from a video posted by an official university account that students used to tease McAfee. The host intimated that the university's promotion of the video made him feel unsafe while filming GameDay on campus, later invoking the school's proximity to Utah Valley University, where Kirk was killed in September 2025.

"And then I thought to myself, has anything like really scary happened at like a college gathering in the state of Utah recently?" McAfee said as part of a longer monologue . "Like, do we think we should be amplifying reasons for why people hate my guts as a university? I don't know."

The fears were backed up in a subsequent statement from ESPN . A spokesperson told The Athletic in part, "We support Pat and recognize the very real and valid concerns he has around safety and security."

The university apologized for the video, which it said "missed the mark."

"We sincerely apologize for creating any perception that Pat was unsafe or unwelcome on our campus," the school said in its own statement.

Following up on Tuesday's news cycle, a report from Front Office Sports added a new level of seriousness to McAfee's assertions. Per FOS, following Kirk's death last September, the FBI advised McAfee to wear a bulletproof vest.

McAfee's appearance on College GameDay that week in Knoxville, TN featured a long opening monologue that alluded to Kirk's death and appealed to the crowd's pride in the country and college football. In the many viral clips from McAfee's speech that Saturday, he doesn't appear to be wearing a vest.

In the past, McAfee has publicized the startling and regular death threats he receives. While not unusual for a public figure in 2026, McAfee's brash character on ESPN and the occasionally charged topics he broaches on air make him a prominent online target. The danger McAfee has worried about before seemingly bled into the real world following Kirk's death, as the country was on high alert for further political violence.

McAfee did not offer any further detail on his comments about the University of Utah during his show Tuesday. GameDay will be in McAfee's backyard this weekend as Indiana hosts Minnesota.

articles.title: “I’m getting to play with these kids": Lewis Hamilton opens up about Kim Kardashian’s kids as speculation about a baby grows
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kim Kardashian’s children, revealing a thoughtful gesture that has brought him closer
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton has offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kim Kardashian’s children, revealing a thoughtful gesture that has brought him closer to her family. The Formula 1 champion shared that he bought a dog named Halo for Kim’s four children, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. His warm comments came as speculation continues about whether the couple could welcome a child together. While neither has confirmed plans to expand their family, Hamilton’s remarks have drawn fresh attention to the bond he is building with the children.Lewis Hamilton reveals his bond with Kim Kardashian’s childrenHamilton opened up about family life while speaking to reporters during an event at the United States Grand Prix in Texas. Asked what brings him happiness away from racing, the seven-time world champion spoke affectionately about his niece and nephew before mentioning Kim’s children.“My niece and nephew always bring me a lot of happiness [and so do] my girlfriend’s kids. I love spending time with them. She’s got four.”He then revealed that he had surprised the children with a pet, giving fans a glimpse of a more personal side of his relationship with the reality star.“I’m getting to play with these kids, and I got them a dog this year. So, little Halo is a new member of that family,” he said.Halo, a golden retriever puppy, has already appeared on Kim’s social media. The gift suggests Hamilton has found a place in the family’s everyday life, although the couple has kept most details of their relationship private.Kim shares four children with her former husband, Kanye West. North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm have occasionally appeared in social media posts featuring Hamilton. The pair knew each other for years before their romance became public, which may have helped make their time together feel more familiar.Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton face renewed baby speculationHamilton’s comments have also revived interest in reports that the couple may want a child together. An August report from Us Weekly, citing an unnamed source, claimed Kim had considered having more children with the British racing driver.“They are really in love. Kim may want to have more kids with Lewis,” the source said. “They just get each other, they get each other’s quirks. She is really happy with him.”The source also described the couple as well matched, saying their shared drive and understanding had helped their relationship.However, the reports remain unconfirmed. Neither Kim nor Hamilton has publicly announced plans to have a baby together, and his latest comments focused on the happiness he finds in spending time with the children she already has.For now, the clearest takeaway is Hamilton’s growing connection with Kim’s family. articles.title: Three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav dies by suicide
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian para-athletics was left in shock after three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav allegedly died by suicide at a flat on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-athletics was left in shock after three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav allegedly died by suicide at a flat on Tuesday night, sources told TOI. The 42-year-old, who competed in the F55 category, suspected to have consumed poison. A postmortem examination was underway at Delhi’s GTB Hospital on Wednesday at the time of filing the report.Who was Neeraj Yadav? - All you need to knowParalympic champion Sumit Antil and fellow para-athlete Vipin Kasana were present at the hospital, sources said. The circumstances surrounding Yadav’s death are yet to be established.India’s chief para-athletics coach S Satyanarayana confirmed the development to TOI, saying he had learnt that Yadav had died by suicide.“Yes, Neeraj has died by suicide. That is what I have also come to know. I have been told that he consumed poison at his flat last night. This is extremely unfortunate and tragic,” Satyanarayana said.The coach suggested that Yadav may have been under emotional distress after missing the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games because of his doping suspension. However, the circumstances that led to his death remain unconfirmed.“He would have been looking forward to competing at these Games. Medals at the Asian Para Games can bring substantial government cash awards and opportunities for stable employment. But his suspension had not ended, and he could not compete. It is possible that this affected him deeply, but we cannot say for certain what he was going through,” Satyanarayana added.Yadav, who hails from Uttar Pradesh, was among India’s accomplished para-athletes. Diagnosed with post-polio residual paralysis at the age of seven, he nevertheless pursued his sporting ambitions. He played wheelchair tennis between 2005 and 2012 before switching to para-athletics.His breakthrough came at the 2015 Delhi State Athletics Meet, where he won gold medals in the shot put, javelin and discus events.Yadav announced himself on the international stage at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, winning gold in the men’s F55 javelin throw with an Asian-record effort of 29.84 metres.He subsequently clinched two gold medals at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games in 2023, winning the javelin and discus events to take his career tally to three Asian Para Games titles.However, his career was clouded by an anti-doping case. The National Anti-Doping Agency provisionally suspended him after an out-of-competition sample collected in Bengaluru in October 2023 tested positive for stanozolol, an anabolic steroid. He later sought DNA testing of his sample through the anti-doping disciplinary process.His death marks a tragic turn in the life of an athlete who overcame significant physical challenges to reach the top of Asian para-athletics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dame Time came to Los Angeles as Trail Blazers hand Lakers first loss of season
articles.summary: Portland shot 50% from 3, got to the line for 40 free throws, and is now 3-0.
articles.body:
"Pretty much every time he shoots, I think it's good," Ja Morant said. "So I'm pretty much bracing for a celebration every time he shoots — but in the fourth quarter, I'm for sure doing it."

"I just lived for those opportunities, you know," Lillard said. "Especially knowing I didn't shoot the ball well (he was 5-of-12), I just loved the opportunity to still be able to do it."

Morant, Lillard and the rest of an athletic, entertaining Portland team can celebrate a 136-129 win over the Lakers that improves the Trail Blazers to 3-0 on the season. This loss was the Lakers' first of the young season.

In a game with a plethora of 3s — the teams combined for 79 attempts — and nearly as many free throws (71), Portland's attack earned them the win. Four Trail Blazers scored more than 20 points: Morant (23), Lillard (21), Deni Avdija (23) and Jrue Holiday enjoyed some home cooking and scored 22 off the bench.

Luka Doncic put up 41 points and had nine assists, while Austin Reaves had 26 points and seven dimes.

These teams were mirror images of each other in some ways — high-powered offenses that attack the rim, and that rely on a big man dropping deep (Walker Kessler and Donovan Clingan) to protect the rim. That defense didn't work for either side in this one, as the Trail Blazers shot 59% on the night — and hit 18-of-36 from beyond the arc — while the Lakers shot 56.3%.

The offenses were firing from the opening tip — the Lakers started game 7-of-8 from the floor. The Trail Blazers shot 71.4% in the first quarter, while the Lakers shot 65%.

How much offense was there in the first half? The Lakers led 72-67 at the break. The Trail Blazers shot 69.7% from the floor and still trailed. The Lakers had a 144 offensive rating, while the Trail Blazers were "only" at 136.7.

That scoring never stopped, but Portland's depth was the one separator in this game. The Trail Blazers had 48 points off the bench, led by Holiday, but Robert Williams III added 14 points, 10 rebounds and some quality rim protection when it mattered.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta reveals Arsenal’s missing trio are injury doubts for Liverpool clash
articles.summary: Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Noni Madueke all missed out on the Fleetwood upset due to fitness problems
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has revealed a triple injury blow for Arsenal in light of their shock Carabao Cup exit to League Two side Fleetwood Town .

The Gunners were beaten on penalties at Fleetwood on Tuesday night after being held to a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes, with Arteta's decision to rotate heavily backfiring.

Injuries forced his hand on some selection decisions, however, with the Spaniard revealing after the match that Declan Rice , Riccardo Calafiori and Noni Madueke all missed out due to fitness problems.

"Riccardo was out, Noni was out with an ankle and Declan Rice was finished with a problem the other day. That's why I had to substitute him [against Everton ]," Arteta said.

The trio could now be doubts for the trip to Liverpool on Sunday, where Arsenal will need to bounce back from cup humiliation.

Their absence compounds Arsenal's growing injury woes this season, with a crisis beginning to develop going forward.

Talismanic winger Bukayo Saka could be out until Christmas after being forced off against Bayern Munich with a thigh injury, joining summer recruit Christos Tzolis on the treatment table.

Madueke's return to form, scoring a late winner at Nottingham Forest earlier this month, was welcomed as Arteta began to operate him on both flanks as a result of injuries, but his own setback will now give the Gunners boss an almighty selection headache.

This will be exacerbated by the suspension of teenager Max Dowman , who will miss the next three games after being sent off for kicking out at a Fleetwood player on a miserable night in the north west.

"I'm sad, I think we are all sad," Arteta said after the match. "We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way.

"It had nothing to do with effort or application or determination to win it, but we lack other things to, to create a much bigger margin than today, with what we produce, they really should have been shown in the scoreline."

articles.title: Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup 2026: Finlay O'Neill on switching from the running game
articles.summary: Finlay O'Neill thought his sporting days were over when his dislocated a knee at the age of 16. Now he is preparing to play a part in England's bid to retain the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.
articles.body:
"If you'd said to me when I was told I couldn't play rugby league again that it's going to be the best thing to ever happen to me, I'd have said 'you're lying'. But discovering wheelchair rugby league, which is even better, has been a blessing."

Rugby league has always been an important part of Finlay O'Neill's life. When he dislocated a knee while playing in a game at the age of 16, he put it down to the rigours of the sport.

The knee popped back into place but continued to cause issues, leaving the Halifax teenager struggling on the field and with increasing pain off it too.

After extensive medical tests, he was diagnosed with shallow kneecaps and hypermobility. His sporting hopes seemed to be over.

But after a lot of family encouragement, he transferred his skills to wheelchair rugby league with Halifax Panthers. Over the past three years, O'Neill has enjoyed a meteoric rise. Now he is part of the England squad who will be defending their Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup title in Australia.

"I think the first thing that really struck me was how similar the wheelchair game is in many ways to the running game," O'Neill, now 21, tells BBC Sport.

"From playing the running game, I had the rugby brain and skill - the ability to pass and see things happening, but I didn't have the physical skill of being able to move in a wheelchair, as I don't use one in my day-to-day life, and that was a big challenge.

"At the reserve or development level, if you've got good rugby knowledge, you can play the game, but you can't just rely on those skills in the Super League. You have to learn how to manipulate the chair and move it around the pitch.

"When you're playing a running sport, you just run and you don't really have to think about it, but in the wheelchair game, you've got to think at the same time about moving your chair to where you want to be, catching a ball, passing it and quickly moving on to the next play.

"At my first Super League training session, I was chasing the others, but playing against quick players means you have to get faster. It has taken a lot of hard work to go from having no chair experience to get up to the skill level of the top players."

News and reports on the BBC Sport website

O'Neill earned his first England call-up in August 2025, playing in the Ashes series in Australia last October and November.

He was then selected alongside Halifax team-mates Jack Brown and Rob Hawkins in coach Tom Coyd's 10-player squad for the World Cup, to take place in Wollongong, south of Sydney.

England start their campaign against Wales on Friday (04:30 BST) before games against the USA and Ireland. Old rivals France, who England beat dramatically in the World Cup final four years ago, are in the other pool alongside Scotland, New Zealand and hosts Australia.

Brown and Hawkins were both part of the team who beat France in 2022 – a final O'Neill watched on television – and the trio helped a dominant Halifax claim a clean sweep of domestic honours for the second season in a row.

"Jack and Rob always say they're each other's biggest rivals and I say I'm the one trying to catch them," he says.

"From training together with Halifax and England, we have that connection and understanding on the pitch.

"One of my strengths is putting players through gaps and I am more of a playmaker than the one breaking through to score amazing tries.

"If I hold the ball a certain way, Jack knows I want him to run under me or go around me and it's the same with Rob.

"I don't necessarily need to talk to them on the pitch. It is just instinct."

O'Neill, who combines his sport with a job at a local supermarket, is one of five England World Cup debutants and is keen to justify the faith placed in him by Coyd and also his Halifax coach Wayne Boardman, who was part of the 2022 team.

"When I got the international call up last year, I said I would give it everything for the next two years to be in contention for the World Cup and I went for it and it has happened," he says.

"I think this is going to be the most competitive World Cup ever. With so many new players involved, it's a completely different sport to four years ago.

"We are very confident going to Australia. As a team we are not going out to defend the title, we are going to win it."

Wheelchair rugby league versus wheelchair rugby - what are the differences?

Wheelchair rugby league - the sport O'Neill plays - was developed in France as a way of bringing the sport to people with disabilities. It is fully inclusive, with disabled and non-disabled players able to play on the same team, and follows many of the same conventions as the running game.

Teams of five players have six tackles to score. Tackles on the ball carrier are made by pulling off an tag attached to each player's shirt. A try scores four points, with two points for penalties and conversions, which are taken by punching the ball off a tee over the posts.

The game is played with an oval ball and lasts for 80 minutes, with a maximum of two non-disabled and three disabled players allowed on the field at any one time.

Wheelchair rugby - which is part of the Paralympic Games programme, and is also known as murderball - is played by those with specific neurological and physical impairments including tetraplegia, cerebral palsy and amputations.

It is played by teams of four using a round ball like a volleyball, and a match consists of four eight-minute quarters.

Athletes are classified with a points system from 0.5 (highest level of impairment) up to 3.5. In international wheelchair rugby, the total number of points of all four athletes playing on court at any one time cannot exceed 8.0, unless there is a woman on the court, in which case the team are allowed an extra 0.5.

To score, an athlete must cross the opposing team's goalline in firm control of the ball. Two wheels must cross the goalline for a score to count. There are no conversions.

Unlike in the league version, no tackling is permitted in wheelchair rugby, but it is a full-contact sport, allowing collisions between players. Athletes must dribble or pass the ball every 10 seconds, with failure to do so resulting in the referee handing possession over to the opposing team.

articles.title: NHL Power Rankings See Bruins, Hurricanes, Stars and Wild in Top 4
articles.summary: It's transition time in the NHL.
articles.body:
Nearly one-quarter of the league's teams—seven of 32, to be exact—entered Tuesday with multiple-game win streaks, yielding significant movements across the board in this week's edition of B/R's NHL Power Rankings.

The hockey staff got together to vote (awarding 32 points for a first-place vote all the way down to one point for a No. 32 tally), and the point totals created the 32-to-1 ranking that follows.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

Statistics updated through games of Monday, Oct. 26.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

Relishing good times is one thing, but the Canucks need to be consistent in recovering from bad ones, according to veteran Brock Boeser. "We need to find a way to respond when they're tilting the ice," he said . "We need to find a way to squash it."

A 0-for-7 power play is never good, but it was particularly bad in a one-goal home loss amid a stretch of three goals scored in three games. Chicago entered Tuesday's games with the league's only single-digit (8.3 percent) conversion rate.

The Flyers lost their first nine (0-6-3) but rallied for three straight wins to begin to right the ship. "We've played to our identity a little bit more, and we're stacking some more shifts," coach Rick Tocchet said . "It's a lot of positive stuff."

Which Teams Are Pretenders or Contenders? 🤔

Drew Doughty has done everything that there is to do in Los Angeles, including two Stanley Cup laps, but the 36-year-old isn't looking for an exit ramp. "I think I can play until over 40," he said . "The Stanley Cup, that's what motivates me."

Goals were hard to come by for the Blue Jackets, who scored fewer than four goals in each game of an eight-game stretch and failed to convert on more than 20 consecutive power-play opportunities. Columbus ranked 29th on the power play (11.5 percent) entering Tuesday.

Break up the surging Flames, who went 4-0 on a homestand in Calgary while outscoring their opponents 14-6. A change of scenery is on tap for Wednesday, when the team makes its first of 2026-27 to visit Battle of Alberta rival Edmonton.

Things didn't go so well in New York against the Rangers and Islanders, or subsequently in New Jersey, but Anaheim bounced back with a win in Philadelphia. "Way better team game (against the Flyers)," forward Leo Carlsson said .

Losing three straight wasn't an ideal way for the Sabres to prep for a California trip that'll finish on Saturday in Los Angeles. "We just got to keep working," defenseman Rasmus Dahlin said . "And I'm sure it will get better here."

Heading outside wasn't a remedy for the Jets, whose Heritage Classic loss to Montreal was their fifth straight (0-3-2). Dawson Mercer debuted with Winnipeg in the game after arriving from New Jersey in the Connor Hellebuyck trade.

The Penguins went 0-for-4 on an extended trip, but they've been a different team back in western Pennsylvania, rattling off wins over Florida (4-0) and Nashville (3-2) heading into a Thursday date with visiting Utah.

Igor Shesterkin's injury meant goaltending was going to be an issue for the Rangers, and it's become one during a three-game skid in which they've allowed 18 goals. Dylan Garand has given up 12 on the last 62 shots he's faced.

A visit from Carolina gave coach Jim Montgomery a chance to give his team some perspective. "Very humbling," he said . "Also, (a) tutorial by the Stanley Cup champions about how to play to who you are, no matter the score."

Going 3-2-1 on a six-game trip would have been acceptable had the Sharks not given up four late goals to lose the finale in Boston. "We had some momentum," goalie Alex Nedeljkovic said , "just let it slip away and didn't finish."

Twenty-four-year-old goalie Michal Postava picked up his first NHL win in memorable fashion on Monday, stopping 25 shots and blanking Edmonton in a shootout on the way to a 4-3 defeat of the Oilers. "It's amazing," he said . "I feel like a kid."

Finding the correct power-play recipe has provided a spike for the Predators, who were 4-of-7 with a man advantage in a 6-2 rout of visiting Colorado. Nashville entered Tuesday with the NHL's No. 3 power play (33.3 percent).

The scuffling continued for the Avs, whose loss in Nashville was their third in four games. "(We talked about using) our skating to check and to attack," coach Jared Bednar said , "and we looked like we were the more sluggish group."

Peter DeBoer won 149 games in Dallas and made three playoff final fours, but he didn't enjoy the return, which ended in a 6-3 loss. "I've done this a few times (in) a few different spots," he said before the game. "Your first game back's always a little special."

A four-game run in which Toronto scored 21 goals ended in Calgary, where Kirill Marchenko left with an injury. Meanwhile, Auston Matthews became the fastest in franchise history to amass 800 points (703 games).

These are not your father's Kraken. Punchless-in-the-past Seattle scored at least three goals in seven straight games, including six against Detroit, before being held to one in a 5-1 loss to visiting Minnesota.

Think the Panthers won't be happy to be home on Friday? Think again. Florida's recent four-game road trip began with losses at Ottawa and Pittsburgh, in which it was outscored 9-1. Florida has won 53 regular-season home games across its two Stanley Cup years.

There's nothing quite like scoring against an old team, and Alex Tuch got that experience twice in Washington's 4-3 defeat of Buffalo. "You always want to score," he said , "and to be able to get the game-winner was pretty special."

Jacob Fowler became the youngest NHL goalie to start and win an outdoor game when his 33 saves helped Montreal beat host Winnipeg at Princess Auto Stadium, home of the CFL's Blue Bombers.

Scoring 12 goals across two home wins was a nice sendoff for a western trip that'll keep the Senators away until November 7. A 7-4 defeat of the Rangers was the first Ottawa win for Jonas Johansson, acquired in September from Tampa Bay.

Ryan Craig leaned on leadership when Vegas faced its first adversity of 2026- 27. "They look at themselves: what can they improve, what can they continue, what can they build on?" he said . "We need to do the same thing as the coaching staff."

Count fellow U.S. Olympic gold medalist Jack Hughes among those excited by the prospect of Connor Hellebuyck as a teammate in New Jersey. "We are lucky to have him," Hughes said . "It's exciting. He's one of the best in the league, right?"

Don't expect a six-game road trip, including visits to Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, New Jersey, Toronto, Montreal, and Ottawa, to concern the Mammoth, who've won four road games this season and were ninth in road wins (21) in 2025-26.

Edmonton's early-season resilience keeps getting tested after Zach Hyman (against Detroit) and Mattias Ekholm (against Carolina) left games with apparent head injuries. The Oilers have dropped consecutive games for the first time in 2026-27.

Nikita Kucherov's Hall of Fame chops are obvious and he took another step toward legend status with an assist against Utah that made him the Lightning's all-time points leader with 1,138 in 890 games, passing Steven Stamkos's 1,137 in 1,082.

Nobody's been hotter lately than the Stars, who shook off early doldrums with a prolonged streak that lifted them above .500 and closer to the top of the Central Division. Their plus-12 goal differential entering Tuesday was third in the league.

Consecutive losses in Alberta weren't the ideal way for the Wild to begin a five-game trip, but they bounced back with wins in Seattle and Vancouver, in which they scored nine goals. "I just liked our push back," coach John Hynes said .

The champs took to the road and picked up seven of a possible 10 points before returning home for a three-game stand. "There's not too many nights where you don't get that (effort)," coach Rod Brind'Amour said .

Going 7-0-1 in eight games is good; scoring four in the third period to steal a win is better for the Bruins. "It's impressive how mature this group is sometimes during certain stages and it's fun to see," captain David Pastrnak said .

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Scariest Mascots in Sports
articles.summary: Horror movies, haunted houses and the nutritional info on the back of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups aren't the only things out there to scare us senseless.
articles.body:
Horror movies, haunted houses and the nutritional info on the back of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups aren't the only things out there to scare us senseless.

Sports mascots would like to terrify us into chronic nightmares as well.

Of course, not all mascots are designed to make our skin crawl. Heck, most of the ones that make us want to scrub our eyes and hippocampuses with toothpaste didn't set out to do so.

Someone somewhere thought they were a good idea—cute, endearing, clever, perhaps even suitable for children.

In every instance that followed, they were hopelessly and hauntingly wrong.

Honorable Mention: Pierre the Pelican (New Orleans Pelicans)

Pierre the Pelican received a rebrand in 2014. The New Orleans Pelicans called it reconstructive surgery to fix a broken beak so that he would look "less scary."

The current iteration is noticeably less terrifying, but not altogether uncreepy . Shooting guard-sized pelicans wearing clown makeup over their feathers doesn't scream "warm and cuddly."

At least we're free from the previous version of Pierre (pictured above). He came straight out of Pet Cemetery , a horrorcore Barney web series or both.

Gritty's scare factor doesn't rocket off the charts until you stare at him for a few beats.

Seven-foot fuzzy orange things with unblinking eyes so piercing they would make Elizabeth Holmes cop to deceiving you are visually and viscerally scarring.

Why doesn't he blink? Why is he so tall? Why doesn't he blink? Is he a Sesame Street outcast? The red-yellow sibling to the purple blob peddling milkshakes ? A Muppet understudy? Why doesn't he blink? How is leering at hockey fans adding value to the sport? Why doesn't he blink? What's with this need for so much social media attention? The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives cast members aren't as obsessed with going viral.

Donald Duck's undead alter ego wouldn't be so hair-raising if not for the orange eyes. They alone make Wild Wing into the titular villain from an animated horror movie—an aquatic cyborg powered by AI who promises his intentions are pure but actually wants to decapitate us all with the blades on his ice skates.

So no, Anaheim Ducks. I would not like to request his appearance at my next event.

University of Utah apologizes to Pat McAfee

8. Sebastian the Ibis (Miami Hurricanes)

The University of Miami has apparently never seen an Ibis or even a picture of one .

Sebastian isn't an Ibis. He's a wilder-eyed Daffy Duck with Eugene Levy's eyebrows and Seagull feathers. He's angry, confused or trying to divide 1,357 by 17 in his head.

That description doesn't sound like it would give you night terrors and/or prevent you from visiting a pond, lake, river, stream, marsh, beach or petting zoo ever again. And yet...

Cartoonishly large heads are always jarring. Purdue Pete's is made worse by the trademark hard hat and serial-killer gloves.

Don't get yourself started on the facial features. They're unsettling.

Purdue Pete is presumably supposed to represent the everyday boilermaker tradesman. Raise your hand if you knew that meant giving him the eyes of Woody from Toy Story and the proportions of Wreck-It Ralph.

Disproportionately enormous heads are always hit-or-miss. When you combine them with five o'clock shadow, caterpillar eyebrows, stick-on mustaches, demon eyes and traffic-cone hat, you get something worse than a miss.

You get Pistol Pete, the cowboy possessed by the world's surliest evil spirit, who prefers unmarked vans to horses and saloons and whose business card is a wanted poster.

A Disney illustrator apparently designed Arizona State's official athletic mascot back in the 1940s. We must presume he wasn't happy at work, because Sparky the Sun Devil looks like he is NC-17 Flounder from The Little Mermaid on PEDs, uses Crest White Strips like chewing tobacco, stole Poseidon's trident, copied Captain Hook's facial hair and converted off-brand Mickey Mouse ears into devil horns.

Also, if you're going to be a "Sun Devil," you should probably nail down the correct hue of the actual sun. Mind you, I'm not rooting for this Big Bird-on-a-mean-streak to be more orange. You can't unsee that.

As is, though, Sparky looks more like Rubber Duck Satan.

Emo-bodybuilder SpongeBob SquarePants isn't as comical to look at as you'd expect.

Wichita State says WuShock is a " big, bad, muscle-bound bundle of wheat ." Squint hard enough, and...you still can't see it.

The hair extensions resemble carpet tassels. The grooves on the side of his face make him look like expired celery. Squidward wants his nose back.

WuShock's facial expression is unreadable. Is he happy? Mad? Excited? Going through protein-powder withdrawals? Protesting against fellow looksmaxxers with larger TikTok followings? It's all so chaotic and creepy.

What happens when you stumble upon a broken-down Chuck E. Cheese animatronic in a landfill, dress it like an Easter Bunny and tack on an ultra-long tongue cut from a felted-wool table runner?

Calgary's resident ghoulish puppy was apparently the first-ever NHL mascot. With results like this, it's shocking he wasn't the last.

I was today-years-old when I learned that Jiminy Cricket-shaped wax candles could be members of the clergy.

Friar Dom's facial expression is often described as a grin. It's more like a sociopathic sneer.

The eyes are soulless, unfeeling. The cheekbones are giving off "got Botox and then immediately tried to swallow a hornet's nest" vibes. The Dominican cowl and robe might fit the character, but they also add to the Resin Reaper aura.

If opposable thumbs had faces, wore clothes and remained in a state of irreversible existential crisis, they'd look like Friar Dom.

1. King Cake Baby (New Orleans Pelicans)

Introduced to the world ( for some reason ) almost 20 years ago, King Cake Baby rose to infamy for looking like a Chucky doll attempting to rebrand himself as a Rugrats character whose scooter runs on infant tears and diaper is filled with Bubonic plague.

There's no explanation for why KCB was ever a vision in someone's head, let alone the official mascot of an NBA team. Then again, people have apparently paid three-digit hourly rates to hang out with Burger King's zombie offspring. Every single one of them should be put on a watchlist.

If you're wondering when the Pelicans retired King Cake Baby, the answer is they didn't. KCB cameos are a seasonal tradition these days —though there's also a chance he's standing behind you right now.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Mikey Lewis: Hull KR star can be England hero after debated selection
articles.summary: Mikey Lewis knows his selection for England's squad at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup was divisive but he's ready to take his chance in Australia.
articles.body:
Nobody understood how divisive England's selection of Mikey Lewis was for the Rugby League World Cup than the man himself.

The 25-year-old was picked by coach Brian McDermott as one of three half-back options alongside Harry Smith and captain George Williams, despite a Super League season pockmarked by inconsistency and disciplinary issues.

Lewis' selection ahead of 2025 Man Of Steel Jake Connor added fuel to the fire; the fact the Hull KR man was then left out of the squad for England's opening defeat to Tonga only added to the feeling of Lewis being more trouble than he was worth.

But Lewis, speaking to media on Wednesday from the England team hotel in Wollongong, said that despite his up-and-down season he never doubted that he had earned his place.

"The way my year went wouldn't be the best. I don't need anyone else to tell me," he said. "I just had to put myself in the shop window. I have earned my spot."

And after all the talk, Lewis has the chance to be the man who helps save England's floundering World Cup hopes.

The 30-12 loss to Tonga has England firmly on the back foot, but they gave themselves a chance last weekend with a crushing 82-0 win over France.

Lewis, named among the interchanges, came on for the final 20 minutes and scored two tries to boost England's points difference – and thus their chances of reaching the semi-finals.

To qualify, England must beat Papua New Guinea on Friday, hope Tonga defeat Samoa on Sunday, and make up a 68-point deficit on the Samoans.

So, piling up the tries is the name of the game for England in what might be their final match in Australia this year – and Lewis, again off the bench, will aim to be the man to provide that flourish.

"I will always represent my country to the best of my ability," Lewis said of his two-try cameo in Perth. "I was told to run with the ball, and I wanted to play with a smile on my face.

"We just have to go out and do what we have planned. It will be a tough game, but we have the strike and desire.

"We have a fighting chance, we believe in that. So, we just have to put the hard work in. It is a unique position, so just enjoy that."

Not even Lewis' biggest detractors will deny he had the speed, skill and power to deliver what England need. His temperament is the question.

In 2026, Lewis scored 17 tries and provided 14 assists in 20 Super League matches. However, he also received four yellow cards – the most of any player in the division.

He started the season on the wrong foot with a deliberate trip of an opponent in Hull KR's shock loss to newly-promoted York Knights. Lewis avoided suspension, but the tone was set.

Then in July came the moment he fell from favour for many England supporters. Lewis was served with a four-game ban for a late tackle and a headbutt in a defeat against Warrington Wolves.

Lewis was sin-binned for the tackle during the match, but he then headbutted a Warrington player in an incident that was initially missed by match officials.

It was expected these aberrations would cost Lewis a World Cup place, but McDermott kept faith – now is the time to reward that.

Lewis has been contrite about his disciplinary problems, admitting his teammates were the ones to suffer, and he is seeking external help to deal with his on-field temperament.

Part of his contrition comes from the undoubtable passion and pride Lewis has about representing his country.

That was clear after his debut in October 2023 against Tonga at St Helens. Lewis was named man of the match after a game-winning display, scoring a try and providing an assist in a 22-18 triumph. His emotional post-match interview showed how much playing and delivering for England meant to him.

That will be on display in Wollongong on Friday, whatever the result means for England's progression or role Lewis has in it.

"Last week the hard work was done, my job was to go and cause havoc - that was my instruction, and I did that," he said

"I might get different instructions this week, but I'll do it, because I am proud to play for my country - 20 minutes is 20 minutes for England, I don't really care it's only 20 minutes."

articles.title: WWE's Growing Cody Rhodes Problem
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes is one of professional wrestling's most recognizable faces, a top WWE star and one of the company's best main-event performers.
articles.body:
Cody Rhodes is one of professional wrestling's most recognizable faces, a top WWE star and one of the company's best main-event performers.

Beloved by millions, he has headlined the industry's biggest shows and established his own legacy alongside those of his legendary father, Dusty, and brother, Dustin.

Yet, as 2026 enters its final months, WWE finds itself facing a growing problem surrounding The American Nightmare—largely through no fault of his own.

What do ya wanna talk about? Let's take a look.

Over two years, Rhodes steadily built toward becoming the top star in professional wrestling, defeating Seth Rollins in a trilogy of acclaimed matches, overcoming a controversial WrestleMania 39 loss and winning back-to-back men's Royal Rumble matches. He finally finished his story by defeating Roman Reigns to win the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship in the main event of WrestleMania 40's second night.

He was a made man, the face of both pro wrestling's No. 1 company and its new era.

Well, when someone reaches such heights and then spends two years in and around the WWE title picture, a certain perception sets in. Rhodes is a champion, has been a champion, and anything he does outside the realm of the championship feels like a step down.

Even if it is a feud with a fellow future Hall of Famer and the man who was instrumental in Rhodes' early development as an on-screen presence and in-ring worker, Randy Orton.

Rhodes has become so synonymous with the gold that a storyline without it—even on the periphery—feels underwhelming for a star of his magnitude.

At the same time, fans had begun to express their displeasure with the second-generation star's constant presence in the title picture, so it was clear WWE Creative had to do something rather than allowing Rhodes to face the backlash of an audience who wanted something different.

Perhaps keeping Rhodes in the title picture without having him hold the gold, while also letting him contend with Orton, would have allowed WWE to have its cake and eat it, too.

Regardless, Rhodes has reached such heights within WWE that, like Attitude Era "Stone Cold" Steve Austin and The Rock, when he is not battling for the top prize in the company, it feels like a step down for the performer, not to mention an empty feud, devoid of stakes.

That is where Rhodes finds himself, and no forcing a different story is going to convince the audience otherwise.

The heart of the Orton story is his attempts to conjure a new, edgier side of Rhodes through taunting and manipulation.

It is almost certainly a response from WWE Creative to the vocal portion of the audience demanding more than the clean-cut babyface side of The American Nightmare.

However, if the company's own history has dictated anything, it is that the edginess fans demand out of their top stars cannot be manufactured in a scripted storyline.

In 2014, the creative team produced a feud in which Bray Wyatt attempted to drag the top babyface to new depths, to unleash a side of himself that fans had never seen before, all so he could prove to the world that everyone had a dark side.

Cena resisted, and the feud never quite hit like fans had hoped for, even if it did provide a cool visual or moment a few times.

In fact, the times Cena showed the greatest edge to his character came nearly a decade earlier, when he fought through pain, suffering, and blood to defeat JBL and Umaga in grueling I Quit and Last Man Standing matches, respectively.

They appreciated his toughness and willingness to fight fire with fire, without the creative team hammering home that he needed to do so to be accepted by the audience or to retain his WWE title.

Fast-forward to now, and we have a similar scenario: Rhodes finds himself on the receiving end of Orton's schemes, seemingly to manufacture some edge for WWE's biggest babyface.

Except we have already seen that edge in much more natural environments.

Edgy was Rhodes fighting through a torn pectoral muscle to beat Rollins inside Hell in a Cell; it was him standing up to The Rock and not backing down when the opportunity to finish his story was at stake. It was telling him to " go f--k yourself " when presented with an offer to sell his soul.

Rhodes even beat Brock Lesnar two out of three times, and one does not slay The Beast Incarnate without a little edge.

Fans already know The American Nightmare can turn it up a notch and show a different side of himself. Anyone who followed him through the independents and into All Elite Wrestling knows there is a different side to Rhodes when the time calls for it.

The audience does not need to be hammered over the head with it through a manufactured storyline that eats up time when the same result could be achieved by letting Rhodes find that inner beast in a match or cut loose on the mic.

Then again, creative meddling is as much responsible for the Rhodes problem as anything.

Rhodes should have won the WWE Championship at WrestleMania 39, but a last-minute creative decision prevented that.

Ultimately, whoever called for it was vindicated when the year-long journey back to the company's biggest match, with its top prize at stake, paid off.

That has not been the case for Rhodes at other points in his run, though.

The Rock returned in 2024 to set up a match with Roman Reigns that damn near cost Rhodes his WWE Championship rematch on the grand stage.

Then there was the ill-fated John Cena heel turn, after Rhodes rebuked The Rock's offer to sell his soul, which unarguably hurt the American Nightmare's story arc. The Travis Scott interference in the WrestleMania 41 main event did not help, either.

There was a flurry of championship changes at the end of 2025 involving Drew McIntyre that hurt Rhodes' standing with the audience, really for the first time.

Oh, and the Pat McAfee debacle that ruined what was the easiest WrestleMania main event to book in years between Rhodes and Orton. What should have been a layup ended with fans intensely booing QB1, even as he fought through blood and nearly lost his eye.

Rarely, if at all, has Rhodes' journey as the guy in WWE felt like it has stayed on track and been everything that it could be, thanks in large part to meddling in his creative, mostly from above the Chief Content Officer's head.

Rather than a legendary run to accompany a two-year journey to the top of the company, Rhodes and his fans have been subject to what feels like a creative fever dream.

The constant interference with his creative, resulting in abrupt changes, alterations, nonsensical twists and turns, and WrestleMania disappointments when he is more than capable of delivering classic encounters, has done more damage to Rhodes and his run as the face of the company than anything.

articles.title: ‘Aye pehelwaan kaisi hai?’: Neeraj Yadav remembered as a friend, motivator and ‘zindadil insaan’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Aye pehelwaan kaisi hai?\" - that is how Suvarna Raj remembers Neeraj Yadav speaking to her.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Aye pehelwaan kaisi hai?" - that is how Suvarna Raj remembers Neeraj Yadav speaking to her. The two para-athletes shared years of training, laughter and memories. For Suvarna, who won gold at the 2026 Asian Para Games, Neeraj was a 'zindadil insaan' - a person full of life who always found ways to encourage others, especially young athletes.The athletics field will no longer echo with his laughter. His fellow athletes will miss the way he waved his hands, called out to them by their familiar nicknames and brought life to every gathering.Neeraj, a three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist, was found dead in Delhi on Tuesday night. Preliminary reports suggested that he may have consumed poison, though the circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear. His body was taken to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital for a postmortem examination, with a police investigation underway.For those who trained with him, he was a friend, a fellow athlete, an elder brother and a source of encouragement. The news of his death left the para-athletics community in shock.Chief coach S Satyanarayana, who was close to Neeraj, struggled to come to terms with the loss.“Neeraj has died by suicide. I was close to him. He was a very good human being. His body is at GTB Hospital. They are yet to hand over the body to us. Tough time for all of us,” Satyanarayana told TimesofIndia.com.‘He was my roommate’For Navdeep Singh, India's Paris Paralympics gold medallist in para-javelin and a bronze medallist at the 2026 Asian Para Games, Neeraj was more than a fellow athlete. He was an elder-brother figure with whom he had shared rooms during training camps and competitions.He was asleep when his phone rang in the early hours of Wednesday. It was fellow para-javelin thrower and Paralympic champion Sumit Antil, who asked him to rush to the hospital and informed him about Neeraj.Navdeep rushed to GTB Hospital, where he learnt that Neeraj had died. The athlete's body was subsequently taken for a postmortem examination as authorities began investigating the circumstances surrounding his death.Recalling their time together, Navdeep said they had shared a room during training in Bengaluru in 2023. They had also travelled together for competitions, including the 2022 IWAS World Games in Portugal.“We were roommates for a long time. We shared a room in Bengaluru when we were training there throughout 2023. Whenever we travelled for competitions, we stayed together. We had also gone to Portugal for the IWAS World Games in 2022,” Navdeep recalled.“We trained together for a long time, from 2021 to 2023. We were part of the same group.”What Navdeep remembers most about Neeraj is his innocence and playful nature. Although Neeraj was older, the two shared an easy friendship filled with jokes and laughter.“He was innocent and had a great sense of humour. He was much older than me, but we never felt that age difference. He would jokingly call me ‘bhai saab’ and use words for me that people usually use for someone older. We were like people of the same age when we were together. We used to joke around a lot and spend a lot of time together. There are so many memories that it is difficult to choose just one or two,” Navdeep said.“We used to go out together whenever either of us had some work. Sometimes we would go to the market for juice or watch movies. He was very fond of films, and I also love watching them. We spent a lot of time together and shared many memories,” he said.‘A zindadil insaan’Suvarna had known Neeraj since the early years of her athletics career. She began training around 2016-17, and the two practised together before travelling to the 2018 Asian Para Games.Even shortly before leaving for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games in Japan, Suvarna was in touch with him. She needed a discus, and Neeraj had offered to help arrange one.She did not know that their conversation would be among their last.“I had spoken to him two days before I left. I needed a discus, and he said he would try to arrange one for me. I left two days later, and we did not speak again,” Suvarna recalled.Neeraj was in Sonipat at the time and had told her that he would try to arrange the equipment.“I had only two days left before leaving. He was in Sonipat and said he would try to arrange it. Now, I keep wondering what happened and why things turned out this way. It is difficult to understand because he was such a strong person,” she said.Suvarna also remembered the way Neeraj spoke to people. His familiar way of addressing her as “pehelwaan” had become a part of their friendship.“We practised together from the time I started my athletics career around 2016-17. We also went to Asia together in 2018. I liked the way he spoke. He had his own style and would always call me ‘pehelwaan’. That was something he said regularly,” she said.“I still cannot come to terms with what has happened. Honestly, it feels as if there is something more to the story and that we are not hearing everything. It is still very difficult for me to believe,” Suvarna said.The athlete who encouraged othersNeeraj competed in the F55 category and was serving a four-year suspension after testing positive for a banned substance, which ruled him out of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya. He was also stripped of the javelin and discus gold medals he had won at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games. The loss of those medals also meant the loss of the associated government cash reward and the prospect of a government job.Diagnosed with post-polio residual paralysis at the age of seven, Neeraj initially took up wheelchair tennis before moving to para-athletics.He won javelin gold at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta with an Asian-record throw of 29.84 metres. At the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, he won gold in both the javelin and discus. Those medals were subsequently stripped following his doping case.For Suvarna, however, it is difficult to reconcile the circumstances of Neeraj's death with the encouragement he continued to offer other athletes. She recalled how he had recently motivated another athlete, Anmol, urging him not to give up and to work towards a comeback.“He was such a strong person and always motivated others. We have an athlete named Anmol, whom Neeraj encouraged just three or four days ago. He motivated Anmol so much that he felt inspired to keep going,” Suvarna said.“Neeraj would tell him not to give up and would encourage him to make a comeback. He would say, ‘Keep doing well. Work hard. Do this, do that.’ He also reminded Anmol that I had won a medal at the age of 44. And then, suddenly, we received this news.”Suvarna said Neeraj had also spoken about returning to competition in 2028. That conversation has made his death even harder for her to understand.“We had never heard that he was depressed because of his sport. I spoke to Anmol early this morning, and he told me that Neeraj had been talking about 2028. He was saying, ‘Just wait and see what I do in 2028, how I make my comeback. Everyone will remember that comeback.’ He was speaking like this only recently,” she added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan’s Rauf sanctioned for conduct contrary to ‘spirit’ of cricket
articles.summary: One demerit point added to the Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf’s disciplinary record for conduct during ODI against England.
articles.body:
Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf has been reprimanded and fined 20 percent of his match fee for “displaying conduct contrary to the spirit of the game” against England, while the visitors were fined for a slow over-rate, the International Cricket Council (ICC) said.

Rauf breached Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct during Sunday’s One-Day International (ODI) tri-series match against England, which Pakistan unexpectedly won by one wicket thanks to batting heroics by Shadab Khan.

He hit the winning run at the end of an 89-run partnership with Shadab to propel Pakistan into the series final, after the home side were reduced to 154-9 in pursuit of England’s 242.

The right-arm fast bowler breached Article 2.2 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to “displaying conduct contrary to the spirit of the game”, according to the ICC.

The incident occurred at the end of the 46th over of Pakistan’s innings, where Rauf appealed for a wide at the non-striker’s end before arguing with England all-rounder Will Jacks.

Per the ICC, Rauf raised his bat and continued the exchange with Jacks despite a warning from umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid. He then brushed past the umpire while walking towards Jacks.

One demerit point was also added to his disciplinary record, bringing the total to five, since this was his third offence within 24 months.

Under ICC rules, four or more demerit points incurred within a 24-month period become two suspension points. That in turn equates to a ban from one Test, two one-day internationals or two T20Is.

Rauf served a ban of two ODIs last year following breaches in three Asia Cup games against India.

The bans will be doubled if Rauf reaches eight demerit points.

Separately, England were fined 15 percent of their match fee for being three overs short of their target after time allowances were taken into account.

Players are fined 5 percent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl within the allowed time, according to Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct.

Rauf and England captain Harry Brook admitted their respective offences and accepted the sanctions proposed by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees. As a result, no formal hearings were required.

The charges were levelled by on-field umpires Rashid Riaz and Sharfuddoula, third umpire Wayne Knights and fourth umpire Nassir Hussain.

Pakistan are through to the two-series final on Saturday, while England take on Sri Lanka on Thursday for a shot at redemption and a chance at making the final after being thrashed by the Lions last week.

articles.title: Real Madrid apologise to Chinese people for Mbappe’s Mao ‘dictator’ remark
articles.summary: Mocking Mao Zedong is taboo in China, which is a lucrative market for players and teams such as Kylian Mbappe’s Real.
articles.body:
La Liga club Real Madrid ⁠⁠issued an apology on Wednesday ⁠⁠after their French superstar Kylian Mbappe triggered a fierce backlash over his comments referring to the former Chinese leader Mao ⁠⁠Zedong as a “dictator”.

After apologies from Mbappe and La Liga failed to quell the negative response in China, La Liga President Javier Tebas set up a crisis unit ⁠⁠and met with Chinese ambassador Yao Jing.

The controversy highlighted the risks for athletes and brands in the lucrative Chinese market, where satire about Mao, modern China’s founding leader, who ruled the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, remains a social taboo.

“Real Madrid CF wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappe,” Real said in a statement.

“Our club maintains a deep respect for China, its history, its culture and its citizens, as well ⁠⁠as for the millions of Chinese fans who ⁠⁠feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid,” the statement added.

China’s state-owned broadcasting platform Migu will not be showing Real Madrid’s La Liga game against Racing Santander on Sunday, while Chinese brands, including dairy companies Mengniu and Shanghai Milkground Food Tech as well as Eastroc Beverage, have ceased ⁠⁠all cooperation with Mbappe.

Migu is scheduled to show nine of La Liga’s 10 games this weekend, with Real Madrid’s match the only ⁠⁠one not covered. Migu did not immediately respond to a request for comment from the Reuters news agency.

La Liga moved quickly ⁠⁠to set up a crisis unit and reached out to Real Madrid, a significant move following years of strained relations between Tebas and the club due to a power struggle within Spanish football. Real Madrid recently called for Tebas’ resignation .

Both parties put aside their differences, acknowledging the potential immediate ⁠⁠and long-term financial repercussions of Mbappe’s comments. Following Real’s statement, sources at La Liga said Tebas was considering travelling to China to neutralise the threat of a huge financial loss for ⁠⁠Spanish football.

La Liga will also consider strengthening its institutional engagement with Beijing amid serious ⁠⁠concerns about a sharp drop in revenue, as Chinese state television awaits further gestures of reconciliation.

In a video on a French podcast that has since been taken down, Mbappe is heard discussing a humorous meme where his face had been photoshopped onto an image he described as “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

Fans have been creating memes superimposing Mbappe’s ⁠⁠face on images of military and political leaders to suggest that he has the power to influence decisions at the teams he plays for. Mbappe has been nicknamed “the dictator” in ‌‌the European press.

On Wednesday, when asked what China thought of Mbappe’s apology , foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said: “We take seriously the apology that ‌‌the ‌‌person has made.”

articles.body: The NHL’s new Hometown Remix jerseys have drawn attention after the website Jersey Nerds reportedly revealed 20 designs ahead of their official release. The leaked looks feature several teams, including the Anaheim Ducks, Detroit Red Wings, Edmonton Oilers, Ottawa Senators, New York Islanders and Minnesota Wild.The early designs have prompted contrasting reactions, with the Anaheim Ducks’ reported throwback-inspired look attracting particular interest. The NHL and Fanatics announced the Hometown Remix program in August, describing it as a special-edition uniform initiative celebrating each team’s fans, city, and local culture. The team has also used the phrase “Oil Country After Midnight” in a promotional teaser, adding to anticipation around the reveal.The Minnesota Wild’s leaked look has also received criticism in the source report. These reactions illustrate the challenge of designing alternate uniforms: some supporters favor familiar logos and traditional colors, while others expect a more dramatic reinterpretation.How NHL Hometown Remix jerseys could connect with fansThe Hometown Remix initiative is intended to connect each franchise’s uniform with its local identity, rather than simply introduce another alternate sweater. The league’s collaboration with Fanatics includes special-edition apparel and headwear alongside the jerseys.For teams, the designs offer an opportunity to celebrate regional culture and create a distinct look for selected games during the 2026–27 season, and for fans, the appeal may depend on whether each jersey feels authentic to the franchise and its community.The leaked images have already started that conversation, but the designs remain subject to official confirmation. articles.standfirst: Un vídeo difundido en redes sociales muestra a varios taxis circulando como si estuvieran compitiendo por algunas de loss carreteras que formaron parte del circuito urbano de Madrid
articles.summary: Un vídeo difundido en redes sociales muestra a varios taxis circulando como si estuvieran compitiendo por algunas de loss carreteras que formaron parte del circuito urbano de Madrid
articles.body: El asfalto por el que hace unos meses rodaron los monoplazas de Fórmula 1 vuelve a tener protagonismo en Madrid, aunque con unos protagonistas bastante distintos. Varios taxistas han aparecido en un vídeo que se ha difundido por redes sociales en el que recorren de noche algunos tramos del Madring como si estuvieran disputando su propia carrera (que no un simple recorrido). El Gran Premio se celebró en septiembre, cuando la capital recuperó una prueba de la máxima categoría del automovilismo con un circuito urbano diseñado alrededor de la zona de Ifema. Una vez terminada la carrera, buena parte de las instalaciones temporales se retiraron, pero algunos tramos del trazado siguen formando parte de las calles por las que circulan los vehículos. Lo que no estaba previsto era que algunos conductores utilizaran esos tramos para correr sus propias carreras, como al parecer han hecho los mencionados taxistas. Así queda patente a la vista de las imágenes que han sido publicadas en redes. El episodio recuerda a otro que se produjo durante la construcción del Madring, cuando unos trabajadores entraron con una furgoneta en una zona todavía en obras y circularon a gran velocidad (para tratarse de una furgoneta) sobre el terreno embarrado. La furgoneta terminó sufriendo un accidente, en una escena que puso de manifiesto el riesgos de utilizar como pista un espacio que no estaba preparado para la circulación normal. En el caso de los taxis, nada se sabe sobre cómo accedieron a la zona o si su actitud llegó a suponer una infracción de tráfico o incluso un delito contra la seguridad vial.

articles.title: Shadman Islam’s 99 leads Bangladesh to 213-3 vs West Indies in first Test
articles.summary: Bad light prevents Shadman Islam from completing century against West Indies in opener of first cricket Test in Mirpur.
articles.body:
Opener Shadman Islam hit an unbeaten 99 to steer Bangladesh to 213-3 on the opening day of the first cricket Test against the West Indies.

The left-hander was on the verge of his third Test century when bad light ended play after 74 overs at the start of the two-match series in Mirpur, Bangladesh.

Shadman hit 10 fours in his 219-ball stay, with Litton Das on 10 not out.

“It was nerve-racking even for us — at the end of the day, the whole team was nervous because everyone wanted him to get to his hundred,” Bangladesh batting coach Mohammad Salahuddin said on Wednesday.

“He has played around 30 (32) Test matches but has only two centuries, and I think that number should have been higher.”

Towhid Hridoy retired hurt on 42 due to cramps after he and Shadman added 88 runs for the fourth wicket to steady the Bangladesh innings.

West Indies struck early when in-form opener Tanzid Hasan edged Jayden Seales to second slip for nine.

Mominul Haque added 28 before falling to Jomel Warrican’s left-arm spin.

Shadman guided Bangladesh to lunch at 96-2, before Warrican struck again shortly after the break to trap Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto leg before wicket for 19.

“Ideally, I would want one more wicket, but we have control of the game. The game never got away from us,” said Warrican.

“We were very disciplined as a bowling group. Even if you’re not getting wickets, you try to be as disciplined as possible. That’s the key, which we did very well. But ideally, we wanted at least one or two more wickets today.”

Shadman brought up his half-century off 95 balls, and he found an able partner in Hridoy, who came into the side in place of the injured Mushfiqur Rahim.

They batted through the afternoon session to take Bangladesh to 177-3 at the tea break.

Hridoy then suffered cramps as he approached his maiden Test fifty and was helped off the field.

Bad light then interrupted play for an hour, with umpires calling off play for the day after a short resumption.

Warrican was the pick of West Indies’ bowlers with 2-33.
