articles.title: Pretenders or Contenders: Which 2026-27 NHL Teams Are For Real?
articles.summary: We've made it to the end of October, and the first month of the NHL season flew by.
articles.body:
We've made it to the end of October, and the first month of the NHL season flew by.

The Hurricanes became the first team to reach 10 wins Tuesday with a heated 2-1 victory over the Bruins, who sit just behind them atop the Eastern Conference standings. The Wild are slowly but surely emerging as favorites in the West, and acquiring Dylan Larkin and extending Quinn Hughes are starting to look like realistic possibilities.

Meanwhile, Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil, debuting in their net Tuesday with a confident 5-1 win over the Stars.

With about a month to go until Thanksgiving, the league's top, middle and bottom tiers are starting to take shape. Some of the teams exceeding expectations could be for real, while others will prove to be pretenders.

The Bruins may have dropped a close one with a 2-1 loss to the Hurricanes in an early battle for the East on Tuesday, but watching that game somehow just made you more confident in both teams.

Jeremy Swayman made 28 saves for a .933 save percentage in the loss. He's rocking a stellar .921 save percentage overall this season, and according to MoneyPuck.com , he's No. 4 among NHL goaltenders right now with 8.2 goals saved above expected.

The Bruins as a whole are looking solid on both ends of the ice, with a 9-3-1 record and the Atlantic Division lead to prove it. They're ranked fourth league-wide with 3.77 goals per game and second league-wide, averaging just 2.15 goals against per game.

New captain David Pastrňák has been doing his thing for seven goals and 18 points in 13 games, and young players like rookie James Hagens (4-5-9 in 13 GP) and 22-year-old Fraser Minten (5-5-10 in 13 games played) are stepping up.

It's hard to find a flaw on this team right now, and while the younger players might run into some scoring slumps, you can expect Swayman to hold it down throughout the season.

Pretender or Contender? Contenders, even in the gauntlet that is the Atlantic Division.

The Devils were surging after a rough start to the season, and everything was starting to fall into place—everything, that is, except goaltending.

While defense was shaping up and players started stepping up offensively, Jake Allen and Nico Daws had been splitting the net, and both were struggling in their own unique ways. Allen had a 3.15 GAA and an .883 save percentage through six games, while Daws had a 2.78 GAA and an .876 save percentage through four games.

In came three-time Vezina winner Connor Hellebuyck, who is arguably still the best goaltender in the league despite coming off a down season. The Devils didn't have to give away any of their consistent producers in the trade, so their scoring-by-committee approach won't be affected.

As for Hellebuyck, he shone in his 5-1 debut over the Stars Tuesday, with 17 saves and a .944 save percentage. The Devils have now strung together a four-game win streak, good for an 8-4-0 record and second place in the Metropolitan Division.

Pretender or Contender?: Contenders, especially if Jack Hughes can stay healthy this season.

The heartbreaking reality of the Igor Shesterkin injury is finally setting in for the Rangers.

They were off to a roaring start, including a goalie goal by Shesterkin and the consistent production they'd been seeking from the younger roster players. Then, Shesterkin went down with an early injury that will keep him out for the rest of the season. The Rangers were able to keep the momentum going for some time, but a 7-1 loss to the Devils on Oct. 15 was the first sign that it wouldn't be sustainable.

At this point, the wheels are coming off. The Rangers have slowly but surely dropped to third in the Metro amidst their current three-game losing streak, with a 7-6-1 record, a 4-5-1 record in their last 10, and a goal differential of plus-2.

They're still in a playoff spot, sure, but it's hard to ignore how directly the Shesterkin injury is starting to have an unfortunate impact on this roster.

Pretender or Contender? : The Rangers aren't pretenders per se, but an injury to one of the best goalies in the league and a lack of confidence make us feel like they are no longer contenders.

The Sharks have become an emerging favorite team for hockey fans new and old due to the rise of superstar Macklin Celebrini, but are they actually going to make the playoffs this year?

They've had an up-and-down start to the season, and the lows feel particularly low. This team has an extremely young core, and it shows, for better and often for worse.

Even strength has become an issue, and while it's great that the Sharks boast a top-10 power play in the league, they're relying on it too much. Lack of even-strength production is a good indicator of underlying struggles, and it tells the story of a fun-to-watch yet incomplete Sharks team.

Right now, San Jose sits at fourth in the Pacific with a 6-6-1 record and a minus-8 goal differential. While Celebrini has been solid with five goals and 15 points in 11 games, the structural issues team-wide are going to take some more experience to figure out.

Pretenders or Contenders?: For now, pretenders. The Sharks could overperform and sneak their way into the playoffs this season, but it will definitely feel more like sneaking in and less like contending if they do so.

Oh, Maple Leafs, what do we make of you one month into the season?

Gavin McKenna has had some rookie moments, but he's finding his groove with three goals and eight points in 14 games.

The stars around him have been shining: Auston Matthews looks invigorated with nine goals and 20 points in 14 games, and Kirill Marchenko was a great acquisition, as he's got six goals and 14 points in 14 games.

Unfortunately, Marchenko got hurt in Monday's game against the Flames and is listed as day-to-day, which would be a huge loss.

Sergei Bobrovsky has been decent enough in his new home, but he's got some room for improvement, with a save percentage below .900.

The Leafs as a whole are hanging in there in a four-way tie for second place in the Atlantic with a 7-5-2 record and a goal differential of six. As usual, though, they're one of the toughest teams to predict in the toughest division to predict.

Pretender or Contender?: Pretender. You'd like to see them capitalize on Matthews' hot start, and you'd like to see Bobrovsky with a sharper overall performance. Based on those two things and the chaos of the Atlantic Division, the Leafs are likely not yet contenders in the McKenna era.

The Mammoth had a great fight in them on their way to the playoffs last season, and that was with star Logan Cooley sidelined due to injury.

Cooley's impact has been growing and growing in this first month of the season; now he's heated up to four goals and 12 points in 13 games. Three Mammoth are operating above a point-per-game clip: Mikhail Sergachev (!), Clayton Keller, and Nick Schmaltz.

Goaltending remains an issue: Karel Vejmelka is the sixth-worst in the league with -4.6 goals saved above expected through 11 games, and his .881 save percentage doesn't help his case. But he's been above .900 in his last two starts, so we'll see if he can turn it around.

Utah has surprisingly emerged early for the No. 2 spot in the hyper-competitive Central with an 8-5-0 record, but it's a tight race.

Pretender or Contender? Contenders, but the competition is fierce, and they have to figure out a way to improve in net. If Vejmelka can turn it around, or if they can outsource to fix their goaltending problem, they've got a chance to contend. If not, the Stars are heating up, and the Avalanche and Predators are right behind them. The Mammoth should try to figure out a solution quickly to keep momentum here.

The Capitals are above .500 and hanging in there at 6-4-0, but sitting at fifth in the Metro, are they showing us what we need to see to deem them legit contenders in Alex Ovechkin's last season?

Although goalie Logan Thompson has returned to practice and is now deemed day-to-day, his lower-body injury sustained last week is still concerning. The team will struggle to make the necessary November divisional push if Thompson is anything but 100 percent.

Meanwhile, Ovechkin has had a rough start with one goal and four points in 10 games, and new acquisition Jordan Kyrou has had a rough time fitting in defensively so far.

Pretender or Contender?: Pretenders. It's early, but it doesn't seem like the Capitals have the juice to contend right now.

articles.title: Boxer Serrano to hang up gloves in Puerto Rico farewell on January 9
articles.summary: Amanda Serrano will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight world boxing titles against Australia’s Skye ⁠Falzon.
articles.body:
Puerto Rico’s seven-division world ‌champion Amanda Serrano will retire after defending her unified featherweight world titles ⁠against Australia’s Skye ⁠Falzon on home soil, in a fight her promoter dubbed “The Last Walk”.

Most Valuable Promotions said Serrano, who holds a 50–4–1 record with 32 ⁠knockouts, will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight world titles on January 9 at Coliseo de Puerto Rico in San Juan.

Puerto Rico’s only undisputed boxing ⁠champion is also gunning for the all-time women’s knockout record, which the 38-year-old jointly shares with American Christy Martin.

“Boxing has been my life and I never could have imagined the journey it would take me and my family on,” Serrano said in a ‌statement.

“From the early days when women’s boxing was fighting for recognition in small theatre shows, to headlining Madison Square Garden in New York, reaching millions of fans around the world on the biggest shows, and helping open doors for the next generation of female fighters … I always believed and I’m proud of everything we’ve accomplished.”

Serrano made history alongside Ireland’s Katie Taylor in 2022 when ⁠they became the first women boxers to headline New ⁠York’s Madison Square Garden.

The highest-profile rivalry in women’s boxing produced a trilogy of fights which Taylor swept via a majority decision in 2025.

A Guinness World Record holder for winning titles across seven weight divisions, ⁠Serrano also became a leading voice for equality in women’s boxing.

In 2023, she competed in the first women’s unified ⁠world championship bout over 12 three-minute rounds, later voluntarily ⁠vacating her WBC title rather than abandoning her commitment to equal rules.

“‘The Last Walk’ is a celebration of an athlete who changed the sport forever … We’re proud to give Amanda the farewell she deserves,” ‌said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

“Saturday, January 9, will mark the end of an extraordinary career inside the ring, but Amanda’s legacy ‌will ‌live on through every female fighter who follows in her footsteps.”

Falzon, who is also 38, holds a 12-2 record with seven knockouts.

articles.title: What is the controversy between Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe and China?
articles.summary: The French superstar’s comments about Mao Zedong have drawn the ire of China, a lucrative market for sports teams.
articles.body:
Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe is at the centre of a controversy in China for his comments on late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, which have not only cost him several commercial deals but have also led to state television scrapping La Liga broadcasts.

The backlash highlighted the risks for athletes and brands ⁠in the lucrative Chinese market, where satire about Mao, modern China’s founding leader who ruled the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, remains a social taboo.

Once hailed as a footballing sensation, Mbappe was widely adored in China until the controversy caused outrage among the country’s 1.4 billion people.

Despite issuing an apology, the French superstar struggled to dissipate anger on Chinese social media on Wednesday.

Al Jazeera breaks down the row between Mbappe and China:

A video circulated online showed France’s 2018 World Cup winner Mbappe apparently joking about a former Chinese leader.

While Mbappe did not name Mao in the video, he appeared to say the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face digitally altered onto that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

The video, which shows Mbappe preparing to go on air, was purportedly filmed in April, as verified by Al Jazeera.

The clip was shared by French football podcast The Bridge and widely circulated on social media on Monday. It has since been taken down.

Fans ‌have previously created memes superimposing Mbappe’s face on images of military and political leaders to suggest that he has the power to influence decisions at the teams he plays for.

Mbappe, who has been nicknamed “the dictator” in the European press, said last month that he acknowledged the humour, but did not like being compared with figures associated with tragedies.

“There’s a part of it that’s funny. You can tell that, for some people, it’s all in good fun. But there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said in an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe.

The “dictator Mbappe” memes began as caricatures of his influence at Paris Saint-Germain, not statements of political allegiance.

By apparently laughing at an ⁠image depicting him as Mao, however, the France captain entered territory in which self-mockery could be perceived as an insult to a country’s founding leader.

Mbappe’s original joke was not reposted – or had been scrubbed – from China’s tightly controlled social media, with state media omitting any references to Mao, saying instead that the footballer had made “inappropriate remarks concerning China”.

But Mbappe has faced a torrent of criticism from China.

“His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated,” wrote one user on social media platform Weibo.

Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe’s account, where he has at least a million followers, preventing him from gaining any new ones.

The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that “the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention”.

What has the Chinese media said about Mbappe?

In China, satire or jokes about Mao are considered disrespectful.

“A remark about an internet meme has triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the ‌‌limits of celebrity influence,” state media outlet China Daily said.

Mbappe – one of the world’s most prominent athletes – has become the latest sports star to fall foul of a faux pas in China.

Many Chinese media outlets condemned Mbappe’s apparent remarks, but did not repeat them.

“What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it,” the state-backed Global Times said.

“The message from Chinese consumers is clear: respect is not optional; one doesn’t get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance.”

Which Chinese brands have cut ties with Mbappe?

The French football star was dropped by two major brands in China: Dongpeng and Mengniu.

Chinese drinks giant Dongpeng said on Tuesday it terminated its contract with Mbappe “with immediate effect”.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” it said in a statement.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with Mbappe, who, until this incident, was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.

Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo.

Offline too, the Mbappe brand appeared to be scrubbed from stores.

The AFP news agency said that when it visited the Adidas flagship store in Beijing’s Sanlitun shopping district, Real Madrid jerseys were available for sale, but none bearing Mbappe’s name.

Mbappe apologised for his “ill-judged” comment, saying he understood it hurt the Chinese people.

“My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” Mbappe wrote in a statement published on his social media accounts on Tuesday.

The 27-year-old said he “reacted to an image of myself” during the interview.

“I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”

The statement was published in French, Mandarin and English.

What has China said in response to Mbappe’s apology?

China said on Wednesday it took “seriously” the apology from Mbappe.

“We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made,” foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing.

Yes. China’s state television has halted broadcasts of all matches and events involving La Liga and Mbappe, and all advertisements involving Mbappe have been removed, the state-backed media outlet The Paper reported on Tuesday.

“Mbappe’s team knew, or should have known, what the true cost of Chinese brand endorsements was all about,” said Terrence Burns, sports sponsorship expert and CEO of the T Burns Sports Group.

Global sporting figures who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors.

China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019.

How has La Liga reacted to their own Mbappe-China crisis?

La Liga President Javier Tebas said that he held a meeting with the ambassador of China in Spain to address the situation and “seek solutions that allow us to overcome this episode”.

“Our commitment is to keep working together so that an individual episode does not harm the important advances achieved nor affect the millions of Chinese fans who follow our competitions,” Tebas said in a statement posted to social media.

“China is and will continue to be a strategic partner for La Liga.”

Earlier on Tuesday, Tebas issued an apology and said ⁠La Liga deeply regretted the alleged comments that caused discomfort and offence in China.

The Reuters news agency reported on Wednesday that Tebas was considering travelling to China to neutralise the threat of a massive financial loss for ⁠Spanish football.

Tebas and Real share a strained relationship due to a power struggle within Spanish football, but both parties have put aside their differences, acknowledging the potential immediate ⁠and long-term financial repercussions of Mbappe’s comments.

What has Real Madrid said about the Mbappe-China controversy?

Real Madrid on ⁠Wednesday ⁠issued an apology.

“Real Madrid CF ‌wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort caused by the recent words of our ⁠player Kylian Mbappe,” Real ⁠said in a statement.

“Our club maintains a deep respect for ⁠China, its history, its culture ⁠and its citizens, ⁠as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who ‌feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid,” the statement ‌added.

articles.body:
The Houston Rockets will be without star center Alperen Sengun for Wednesday night's matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks as they attempt to continue their undefeated start to the 2026-27 season.

Houston's latest injury report Wednesday morning ruled Sengun out because of low back soreness. The Rockets will begin a two-game road trip against Milwaukee at 8 p.m. ET after improving to 4-0 with Monday night's 120-110 victory over the Atlanta Hawks .

Sengun's absence comes after one of his strongest performances of the young season. The 24-year-old nearly recorded a triple-double against Atlanta, finishing with 29 points, nine rebounds and nine assists. He also collected six steals and one block while shooting 11-for-15 from the field, making his lone 3-point attempt and going 6-for-8 at the free-throw line across 37 minutes.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Through four games, Sengun is averaging a career-high 24.5 points, nine rebounds, seven assists and 1.8 steals per game. He has shot 58.1% from the field and 66.7% from beyond the arc while averaging 34 minutes per contest.

His absence leaves Houston without one of its primary offensive hubs against Milwaukee and creates another frontcourt concern for head coach Ime Udoka.

Rockets will be shorthanded against Bucks

Steven Adams will also miss Wednesday's contest with a right soleus strain, leaving the Rockets without their top two traditional centers.

Marcus Smart , meanwhile, remains questionable because of a left forearm strain. His final status could further impact Houston's rotation against the Bucks.

Two-way players Quadir Copeland and Julian Phillips are also listed as out because of their G League assignments.

The Rockets' full injury report lists Adams, Copeland, Phillips and Sengun as out, with Smart questionable.

Houston has opened the season with four consecutive victories, including back-to-back wins over Atlanta, despite already managing several injuries across its rotation. Kevin Durant and the Rockets will now attempt to preserve their unbeaten record without Sengun anchoring the frontcourt.

Wednesday's game begins a two-game road trip for Houston before the Rockets travel to face the Dallas Mavericks on Friday.

articles.body:
The Minnesota Wild just concluded a five-game road trip, going 3-1-1. One of the major reasons for the success was the play of Quinn Hughes . On Sunday, Hughes scored the game-winning goal for the Wild against his former team, the Vancouver Canucks. On Tuesday night, he added another two points against the Utah Mammoth in the 3-1 win.

With another two points for the Wild, Hughes is setting a franchise record , according to Michael Russo of The Athletic.

"Quinn Hughes (62 GP) became the fastest player in Wild history to record 20 multi-point games with the franchise, surpassing Pavol Demitra (66 GP)," Russo posted on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Hughes has played 14 of those 62 games this season, with the other 48 coming last year. He already has six multi-point games this season. Demitra set the franchise record when he joined the team for the 2006-07 season. He played just two seasons with the Wild before heading to the Canucks.

Meanwhile, Hughes is also having a historic start for a defenseman.

"Quinn Hughes (3-15—18 in 14 GP) became the third defenseman since 1992-93 to record 18-plus points in a single October, following John Carlson (7-16—23 in 2019) and Cale Makar (4-15—19 in 2024)," Russo added.

Hughes has three goals with 15 assists this year, giving him 18 total points. John Carlson has the record for most points by a blueliner in October, racking up 23 points in 2019 with the Washington Capitals. Cale Makar is second with his 19 points in 2024 with the Colorado Avalanche.

Hughes has one more game in October to pass Makar and Carlson, as the Wild host the New York Islanders on Thursday. Meanwhile, another blueliner is also having a historic start this year. Edmonton Oilers defenseman Evan Bouchard, who scored a game-winning goal against the Wild this year, has already racked up 21 points. Five of those points came in September when he put up three goals and two assists against the Canucks on the NHL's opening night. Bouchard has 16 points in October and has two games left to try to catch the three men in front of him for history.

articles.title: Brewers' Joey Ortiz Takes Accountability After Rare Error
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers lost Game 4 of the World Series, and Joey Ortiz made a costly error in the 12th inning
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers were three outs away from a World Series sweep after a clutch home run by Cooper Pratt in the top of the 12th inning.

In the bottom of the inning, Junior Caminero was leading off, and Antonio Senzatela induced a ground ball that went right to Joey Ortiz. He made the throw across the diamond, but it was short, and Jake Bauers could not pick it. Ortiz might be the best defensive third baseman in baseball, and nobody expected him to make an error like that.

"There's no excuse," Ortiz said after the game, per MLB.com's Adam McCalvy . "Not one at all. I should make that play every (expletive) time."

Ortiz's glove kept him in the lineup for most of the season before he had one of the most dramatic turnarounds ever at the plate. He went from the worst hitter in baseball to finishing with a .270/.328/.402 slash line. From July 4 on, he had a .909 OPS.

In the postseason, he has not hit well, and Pat Murphy has gone back to using David Hamilton more. Ortiz has started against only left-handed pitchers since the National League Championship Series, and has not started a game in the World Series.

He is being used as a defensive replacement right now, and he was in the game for Hamilton, who was pinch-hit for by Andrew Vaughn earlier in the game. Had he made the play to get Caminero, there's no telling what would have happened after that. It would have changed the complexion of the inning and taken a ton of pressure off Shane Drohan.

"I fielded the ball and I think I should have took another couple more steps toward first," Ortiz told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's Todd Rosiak . "I made a (expletive) throw."

articles.title: That gothic feeling — Charlie’s Film Room Week 8
articles.summary: Another week, another win.
articles.body:
This is not the same Northwestern team of old. While that has been evident this season, it continues to be proven as the Wildcats enter their toughest stretch of the season. Rutgers isn't that good of a team, but the 'Cats did do a fantastic job of containing KJ Duff, who had his worst output of the season. Offensively, Aidan Chiles threw his first interception of the season, but also scored five total touchdowns. He is the ideal player in this Chip Kelly offense, and it keeps showing up on film.

Chiles has been very, very solid as a passer this season. He's improved his accuracy from when he played at both Oregon State and Michigan State, and he throws one of the most catchable deep balls in the FBS. The Wildcats have the best deep-passing attack in the country, completing over 61% of their deep throws. One of the most impressive things watching the tape besides Chiles is seeing how Griffin Wilde is almost always open, even when defenses know he's likely to be targeted. Wilde hasn't dropped a pass this season either, which speaks to his ball skills and again, his ability to get open.

On the first play, Wilde runs a corner route to the right corner of the end zone, and Chiles uses the play-action fake to buy himself enough time to allow Wilde to come open. Wilde gets a step on the safety and Chiles puts the ball to where only Wilde can make a play on it. The second play is another Chiles —> Wilde pass. Even with three defenders around him, Wilde finds the hole in the zone on the deep out route, and Chiles puts the throw on the money. Chiles on this play doesn't go through progressions as Wilde was the first read, but he has all the time necessary to do so if needed; something he doesn't always have the luxury of having.

The third play is a shot up the seam against man defense. Wilde makes one small cut in his route to turn it into more of a post than a 9 route, but he beats his defender off that break and Chiles feeds it to him on the inside where the defender was trailing from the outside. The fifth play is a shallow cross concept, with Hayden Eligon II running a curl on the left, Wilde running a post on the right and Alex Honig running a drag route from his initial spot inline on the right. The play-action gets the defense to bite enough to the right side of the field, allowing for Honig to spring wide open on the drag. Great play design.

The sixth and seventh plays are both examples of Chiles' improvisation. He sees the pocket collapse on both, takes off with his legs, but stays behind the line of scrimmage long enough to make a throw. Despite his ability to scramble for yardage gains, Chiles wants to pass first before he tucks it and runs. These two plays show that. The threat of him taking off causes defenses to allocate an extra guy to watch him, which allows for receivers to get open more easily against fewer defenders.

It feels like I've included this same play every week. The first play of this cutup is one of the most effective plays by any team this season. Chiles' success rate on short-yardage designed runs this season with a relatively large sample for a quarterback is tremendous. He does such a great job both sneaking it inside, but also reading these sneak plays to instead bounce it outside. This one is more of a straight design for him to bounce it outside, but he does initially extend the ball out for a fake to Gavin Sawchuk, adding an extra possible wrinkle to this play with a potential counter/draw handoff.

The second play, Chiles keeps it himself on a speed option. He's been exceptional this season at deciding when to keep the ball versus when to hand it off on read-option plays. Even though this gain isn't anything super crazy, he does a great job reading the defense here while also taking his time to read the blocking so he can make the cutback.

The final play here, whether it was designed to be a keeper the whole way or a read option, the fake did such a great job that the camera followed the running back. Chiles' fake to Sawchuk got the entire Rutgers defense to bite, giving Chiles the right side of the field all to himself for the walk-in touchdown.

Caleb Komolafe had multiple explosive runs in this game. Northwestern's rushing attack has been very successful in generating explosive runs, with Komolafe in this game averaging 11.5 yards per carry. Per puntandrally.com, Komolafe is averaging 4.18 yards after contact this season, which is T-35th in the FBS and T-6th in the Big Ten.

On this first play, Komolafe spins out of a tackle early and then breaks into the open field. For Joseph Himon II as well, breaking an initial tackle and having green grass ahead is a recipe for disaster for opposing defenses with both their top-end speeds. On the second play, Patrick Schaller does a great job of clearing the C-gap for Komolafe to break into the second level. Schaller has been a bit of a revelation at left tackle, especially considering he was a tight end last season and got his first-ever start at the position against Penn State.

This third play, it's Schaller and Honig who are the main blockers that allow Komolafe to cut back to the left around the line and find daylight. The fourth play is the only of these clips where Komolafe breaks a run going right the whole time, using Grant Seagren's block at right tackle to give him the extra second to get around the pursuing defender.

articles.title: Ravens release Week 8 depth chart ahead of showdown with Bills
articles.summary: The Ravens' Week 8 depth chart reveals key questions at quarterback, center and right guard ahead of Sunday's AFC matchup against the Bills
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will look to rebound from consecutive losses as they travel to Buffalo for a Week 8 matchup against the Bills , and their latest depth chart raises several key personnel questions ahead of Sunday's AFC showdown.

Baltimore (4-3) is coming off a 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals after allowing 35 unanswered points in the second half. The Ravens have dropped consecutive AFC North matchups and now face another difficult opponent as they attempt to regain momentum in the conference standings. The Ravens' biggest questions remain on offense, where injuries to quarterback Lamar Jackson and offensive linemen Ronnie Stanley and Vega Ioane have complicated the team's efforts to establish consistency.

Jackson obviously remains listed as Baltimore's starting quarterback, with Tyler Huntley second and Joe Fagnano third. The offensive line features Ronnie Stanley at left tackle, John Simpson at left guard, Vega Ioane at center, Andrew Vorhees at right guard, and Roger Rosengarten at right tackle.

After Ioane suffered an MCL sprain in the loss to Cincinnati, Andrew Vorhees or Emery Jones will start. Although he remains listed at center, his availability could influence multiple positions along Baltimore's offensive front.

Defensively, Trey Hendrickson remains the team's top rush linebacker, with Mike Green listed behind him. The secondary features Marlon Humphrey, Nate Wiggins, Kyle Hamilton, Jaylinn Hawkins (injured), and Malaki Starks, giving defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver several versatile options against Buffalo's passing attack.

Here is Baltimore's Week 8 depth chart, followed by seven takeaways from the latest personnel listings.

8 takeaways from the Ravens' Week 8 depth chart

1. Cam Jurgens is firmly established as the starting center

One of the most important developments for Baltimore's offense is Jurgens' presence atop the center depth chart after the Ravens acquired him in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles. Jurgens made his Baltimore debut against Cincinnati after spending time in the concussion protocol, giving the Ravens a veteran option at a position that had changed significantly in the first half of the season.

Baltimore previously relied on Ioane at center after injuries depleted its depth at the position. The rookie performed well despite moving away from his natural right guard spot, providing stability while the team waited for Jurgens to become available.

With Jurgens now starting at center, the Ravens have a chance to build continuity on an offensive line that has struggled with injuries. His experience will be key to communication, identifying defensive pressure, and opening running lanes for Henry.

The bigger question is whether Baltimore can keep the same five offensive linemen together long enough to establish the consistency necessary for a productive second half of the season.

2. Vega Ioane remains the starting right guard despite his MCL sprain

Ioane remains listed as Baltimore's starting right guard, with Emery Jones Jr. second and Kyle Hergel third. However, the Ravens may need to use another combination after the rookie suffered an MCL sprain during Sunday's loss to Cincinnati. Ioane is expected to miss time after sustaining the injury in the first quarter. Jones replaced him against the Bengals, making him an important player to monitor as Baltimore prepares for Buffalo. Reuters+1

The injury is particularly frustrating because Baltimore finally had an opportunity to pair Jurgens at center with Ioane at his natural right guard position. The combination lasted less than a quarter before the Ravens were forced to adjust.

Ioane, the No. 14 overall selection in the 2026 NFL draft, had already demonstrated his versatility by filling in at center. His return to right guard was expected to balance Baltimore's offensive front, but the injury creates another potential obstacle.

Jones is the next player listed at right guard, while Hergel provides additional interior depth. The Ravens will need to determine whether Jones can provide sufficient consistency if Ioane is unavailable against Buffalo.

3. Ronnie Stanley and Carson Vinson remain central to the tackle situation

Stanley remains Baltimore's starting left tackle, with Vinson serving as his backup. Roger Rosengarten is listed as the starting right tackle, with Vinson also appearing as his primary reserve. The alignment highlights Vinson's importance as Baltimore's swing tackle, particularly after Stanley exited Sunday's loss to Cincinnati.

Stanley has been one of the Ravens' most important offensive linemen throughout his career, and his health will be critical against a Buffalo defense capable of generating pressure.

Vinson was called upon against the Bengals, gaining another opportunity to handle meaningful snaps on the left side. His development gives Baltimore flexibility, but the Ravens need more stability on the offensive line after frequent changes over seven games.

With Jackson dealing with an ankle injury and Huntley handling starting duties in his absence, dependable tackle play will be essential regardless of who starts at quarterback.

4. Lamar Jackson remains QB1, but Tyler Huntley must be prepared

Jackson remains listed as Baltimore's starting quarterback, with Huntley second and Fagnano third. However, his ankle injury remains one of the team's biggest concerns heading into Sunday's matchup against the Bills.

Jackson has missed three straight games while recovering, leaving Huntley to lead an offense that has been inconsistent over the past two weeks.

Baltimore managed just 10 points against Cleveland and 13 against Cincinnati, struggling to sustain drives and generate explosive plays when opportunities arose.

Huntley has provided experience and familiarity with the offense, but the Ravens have not consistently capitalized on their offensive talent during Jackson's absence.

Jackson's return would give offensive coordinator Declan Doyle another dimension to his attack, especially with the quarterback's ability to threaten defenses as both a passer and runner.

For now, the depth chart confirms Jackson's standing within the quarterback room rather than his availability against Buffalo. His practice participation and injury designation will determine whether the Ravens can get their starter back on the field.

5. Mike Green's starting role gives Baltimore flexibility at linebacker

One of the more interesting developments on Baltimore's defensive depth chart is Green's placement as the starting strongside linebacker, ahead of Zion Young and Ethan Burke.

Green is also listed as Hendrickson's primary backup at rush linebacker, giving defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver another option when building different defensive packages. The alignment is notable because Tavius Robinson suffered a season-ending pectoral injury, creating additional opportunities for Baltimore's younger outside linebackers.

Green's ability to line up in different spots lets the Ravens maintain flexibility with their pass-rushing personnel, especially when Hendrickson is on the field.

Baltimore will need improved defensive execution after allowing Cincinnati to score touchdowns on five consecutive second-half possessions. Green's development could become increasingly important as the Ravens try to generate consistent pressure and finish defensive series.

6. Zay Flowers continues to lead the receiving corps

Flowers remains Baltimore's top receiver, with Devontez Walker and Elijah Sarratt listed behind him. Bateman occupies the other starting receiver spot, followed by Ja'Kobi Lane and Wester.

The receiving group will be under scrutiny entering Week 8 after Baltimore's offense struggled to score in consecutive losses.

Flowers was one of the few bright spots against Cincinnati, finishing with eight receptions for 137 yards and a touchdown. He provided Baltimore with its most explosive plays, but the Ravens couldn't sustain that production after halftime.

Bateman remains important as Baltimore works to develop more consistent outside production, while Walker and Lane provide additional options in the passing game.

Lane's return after wrist surgery gives the Ravens another young receiver who can contribute, and the rookie's opportunities could expand as he gets more comfortable in Doyle's offense.

Baltimore needs more consistent contributions from the entire group rather than relying primarily on Flowers to create explosive plays.

7. Kyle Hamilton leads a secondary looking to rebound

Hamilton remains listed at defensive back, with Keyon Martin and Chandler Rivers behind him. Hawkins starts at strong safety, while second-year safety Starks is listed at free safety.

Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins remain Baltimore's starting outside cornerbacks, with Chidobe Awuzie as the primary backup behind them.

Hamilton's versatility remains one of Baltimore's most important defensive assets. His ability to line up near the line of scrimmage, cover tight ends and receivers, and handle deeper coverage responsibilities gives Weaver flexibility in building different defensive packages.

The Ravens will need that versatility against Buffalo, particularly after struggling to contain Cincinnati's passing attack during the second half of Sunday's loss.

Hawkins' health also warrants attention after a knee injury kept him out against the Bengals. Keondre Jackson appears as the second option at both safety spots, while K'Von Wallace provides additional depth.

Baltimore must improve its communication and execution in the secondary after allowing Cincinnati to turn a 13-point halftime deficit into a comfortable victory.

8. Tyler Loop remains the kicker, with LaJohntay Wester leading the return game

Baltimore's special teams depth chart remains anchored by Loop at kicker, Eckley at punter and holder, and Nick Moore at long snapper.

Loop's performance will remain a storyline after missed field goals contributed to Baltimore's recent struggles. The Ravens signed veteran Jake Moody to their practice squad, but Loop remains the kicker listed on the team's official depth chart.

Adding Moody provides depth and competition without changing Baltimore's primary kicking responsibilities. Wester remains the top kickoff and punt returner, with Ali and Hill as additional kickoff-return options. Sarratt is listed as Wester's backup on punt returns. The Ravens have struggled to consistently capitalize on scoring opportunities during their two-game losing streak, making special teams execution particularly important against Buffalo.

Field position, reliable kicking, and limiting mistakes in the return game could make the difference in a matchup between two AFC teams trying to improve their postseason positioning.

articles.title: Oregon finding value in outside eyes for help assessing struggles
articles.summary: In the midst of a disappointing season, the Ducks' coaching staff has looked to outside eyes for help in turning the season around.
articles.body:
A 4-3 start to the season would be solid for a majority of teams in college football. But when the Oregon Ducks face that situation, the sky is falling. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired on Sunday, to be replaced by assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson. That news preceded the announcement that Dante Moore is unlikely to return to the field this season, potentially ending his tenure as a Duck.

The play-calling change and Moore's decision came just weeks after wide receiver Evan Stewart was detained for a DUII. A week later, true freshmen wide receiver Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott were late scratches and didn't make the trip to Champaign to face Illinois despite a depleted receiver room. The Ducks lost, 21-10, dropping their third game before the calendar has flipped to November.

The product off the field is an issue, but one that head coach Dan Lanning consistently says he'll handle in-house. The product on the field has been an issue as well, as the Ducks have scored 14.0 points per game over the last three games. They've been one of the worst offenses in the nation, with a clear disconnect occurring between the scheme and numerous blue-chippers across the 11 positions.

While Mehringer was fired, the Oregon coaching staff is still searching for what the disconnect has been, even looking for outside perspectives.

"Yeah, in some ways, it's something we've done too," Lanning said when asked about welcoming outside eyes on his team. "It's just not something that you guys would necessarily know about. The great thing about today's technology is there's the ability to Zoom, evaluate film from a distance, right? Put different eyes and perspectives on some of the stuff that we've done."

In the past, Lanning has talked about collaborating with other coaches during the offseason on how they run their programs, name-dropping Clemson's Dabo Swinney. Lanning also visited a Seattle Seahawks practice during Oregon's bye week. Coming from Alabama's staff under Nick Saban, there's no doubt that Lanning has a thorough contact list to choose from if he wants other coaches to take a look at his team.

And if the Ducks in crisis mode and the Oregon staff unable to turn around the ship just yet, Lanning has called on outside perspectives to give him a hand.

articles.title: Patriots trade deadline tracker: News and rumors ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline
articles.summary: Tracking all the relevant developments ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first two months of the regular season.

While the expectation is that they will get several players back from injured reserve at some point, they also could go for a more radical approach in hopes of improving their team and gearing up for a stretch run in 2026. Like they have done multiple times in 2026 already, they could look at the trade market.

Will there be additions to a list that already includes the likes of A.J. Brown, Jaylen Reed, Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse? Or could they move on from some of their players, like they did in 2025 ?

We will know soon: the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET. Until then, please make sure to bookmark and regularly revisit our Patriots trade deadline tracker for all the latest developments.

articles.title: Cincinnati Bearcats can tie 18-year mark with victory over No. 6 Utah?
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bearcats could make it back-to-back top 10 wins with a victory over No. 6 Utah Oct. 31 at Nippert Stadium
articles.body:
After shocking the Big 12 with a 37-24 thrashing of then-No. 8 Texas Tech last weekend, the Cincinnati Bearcats have another chance to take down a Top 10 team with the No. 6 Utah Utes in town for Halloween festivities at 3:45 Oct. 31 on ESPN.

A win would give UC back-to-back Top 10 wins and back-to-back victories over ranked teams for the first time in 18 years. In 2008, the Bearcats coached by Brian Kelly beat No. 23 USF 24-10 on Oct. 30, then eeked out a game in overtime against No. 20 West Virginia, 26-23.

Kelly also had back-to-back ranked wins in 2007, winning at No. 20 USF Nov. 3, then beating No. 16 Connecticut Nov. 10 at Nippert.

Photos: Cincinnati Bearcats host Texas Tech for Homecoming game

UC Bearcats have chance at 4 Top 25 wins

Should the Bearcats knock off the Utes, they have No. 18 Houston on the road Nov. 7 and the regular season finale at No. 8 BYU Nov. 28.

In 2009, former coach Kelly recorded four ranked wins in his final season, winning at No. 24 Oregon State, at No. 21 USF, against No. 23 West Virginia and the famous "Pike to Binns" game at No. 14 Pitt .

In addition to Cole Tabb and MJ Cannon being named Big 12 Offensive and Defensive Players of the Week, respectively, and both sides of the line being honored, Pro Football Focus also recognized some Bearcats.

Defensive backs Jasper Beeler and Kenny Worthy joined Tabb and Cannon on the PFF Big 12 Team of the Week. Cannon's forced fumble, interception and eight tackles put him on the PFF National Team of the Week. Tabb also earned Doak Walker Award Offensive Player of the Week for his 173-yard, two-touchdown game vs. Texas Tech, while Cannon received the Walter Camp Award Defensive Player of the Week for his key forced fumble and interception.

"Cole Tabb's had a great season for us," UC head coach Scott Satterfield said. "You think about what he's done in just about every game. He's a big play threat, our biggest play guy we have on offense. MJ Cannon, what a game he had. We really missed him in that fourth quarter at West Virginia."

Said receiver Larenzo Fenner, "Cole Tabb is a great running back. You ought to see him when he doesn't have the ball in his hand; he plays the same way as when the ball's in his hand. He's a great player to play with."

Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Utah Utes football history

Short and sweet, Utah plowed UC last Nov. 1, 45-14. The Bearcats had 427 yards of total offense, but not much to show for it on the scoreboard.

Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Utah scouting report

Why Cincinnati Bearcats have an advantage: A sellout crowd enjoyed Homecoming at Nippert Stadium with the upset win and that should lead to another packed house. The trick would be outgaining the Utes, who have the No. 8 rushing defense in the country, allowing just 88.3 yards per game. The treat would be another effective throwing game for quarterback JC French IV.

Morgan Scalley, Utah's head coach, was defensive coordinator a year ago and held Brendan Sorsby to 11-for-33 passing at Rice-Eccles Stadium. That atmosphere was wild and the noise bounced off the Wasatch Mountain Range.

The UC student section should be packed to the gills again and could amplify a scary night if they can throw off signals as they did vs. Texas Tech.

"The way the students performed last Saturday was great," linebacker Simeon Coleman said. "It definitely had an impact on us winning that game."

Coleman mentioned that when Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond fumbled early in the game, he felt the stadium shake.

"It was definitely the top experience in 'The Nipp' since I've been here," he said.

There's also the time zone issue, as teams crossing two time zones East to West or West to East often struggle. Just ask BYU, which went from knocking off Notre Dame in Provo to getting upset in Orlando in overtime

Why Utah has an advantage: Utah quarterback Devon Dampier threw for 213 yards and two touchdowns last year and ran for 78 yards. Backup Byrd Ficklin is equally as dangerous, and the two have combined to run for over 500 yards. Then there's Wayshawn Parker, who had 104 yards a year ago and, like UC's Cole Tabb, can catch and run. Parker and Tabb both have 12 touchdowns.

"Last year, going out and playing those guys, we really didn't slow'em down very much," Satterfield said. "They do so much in stretching the defense horizontally from sideline to sideline and it creates some thin areas in your defense. Also, they can push the ball downfield throwing it."

It's another game where Utah is tough up front, and the Bearcats are going to have to win the battle in the trenches.

"Houston moved the ball on them and just didn't score enough points," Satterfield said. "You're going to have to get some tough yards. There's going to be some dirty runs and some pass plays that are not very clean. You're just going to have to try and win some of those."

Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Utah injury report

The Bearcats played without nose tackle Josh Hough and running back Gi'Bran Payne against Texas Tech as both were injured in the loss at West Virginia. Satterfield expects Payne to be back, while Hough has improved and has a chance to play.

Redshirt freshman receiver Giyahni Kontosis suffered a torn ACL against the Red Raiders and will miss the remainder of the season. UC center Taran Tyo left the Texas Tech game, then briefly returned with a hand injury. Grant Edgington filled in admirably, and both should be ready against Utah.

articles.title: College Football Player and Son of Former NFLer Kicked Off Team After Being Accused of Harassing Cop Online
articles.summary: Dee Kirkpatrick Jr. was arrested last November after he allegedly fled from officers who pulled him over for speeding
articles.body:
Dee Kirkpatrick Jr. is no longer with the Alabama football team

The defensive back was arrested on Friday on two misdemeanors involving a police officer who was connected to Kirkpatrick's previous arrest last year

Kirkpatrick was arrested in November 2025 on three counts of reckless endangerment, attempting to elude, and speeding

Alabama football has parted ways with Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. one year after he allegedly fled from officers during a traffic stop and days after he was arrested on accusations of doxing the police officer involved in the initial charges.

The defensive back, 20, was already suspended over a violation of team rules before last week's win over Texas A&M, a university spokesperson confirmed to The Athletic .

"He's not with us," Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer said in a news conference Monday . "We just have an expectation and standard in our program and the team rules and things that go along with that. There's still some details that I'm trying to understand, but it's enough to where we know that's not how we operate."

Kirkpatrick was arrested on misdemeanor charges on Friday, Oct. 23 after a University of Alabama police officer alleged to authorities that he received a profanity-laced Facebook Messenger communication from Kirkpatrick on Oct. 20.

According to the court documents filed on Monday and obtained by The Athletic, the officer claimed that he then went to Kirkpatrick's Facebook page to block him and found a photo of himself, his wife and their two children posted, with a caption that read, "Dis him?"

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

The officer was concerned for his safety and that of his family, the court documents said.

The officer conducted a traffic stop in November 2025 on the Strip in Tuscaloosa in which Kirkpatrick allegedly fled and eluded officers at the scene, according to the Tuscaloosa Thread .

Kirkpatrick was charged with three counts of reckless endangerment, attempting to elude, and speeding. He was suspended for the last seven games of the 2025 season.

The Gadsden, Ala. native is the son of former NFL Dre Kirkpatrick, 37, a cornerback who played for the Cincinnati Bengals and Arizona Cardinals for 10 seasons.

The younger Kirkpatrick played in Alabama's first seven games of this season, recording five tackles and one forced fumble.

articles.title: Detroit Red Wings Get Bad News on Three Injured Players
articles.summary: Todd McLellan provides injury updates on Albert Johansson, Marco Kasper, Mason Appleton, and Dylan Larkin ahead of Detroit's next game.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings are coming off an impressive shootout victory over the Edmonton Oilers, but head coach Todd McLellan delivered some unfortunate injury news Wednesday afternoon.

Defenseman Albert Johansson has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Chicago Blackhawks, while forwards Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton remain approximately two weeks away from returning.

There was, however, some encouraging news regarding Dylan Larkin.

Albert Johansson Ruled Out, No Return Timeline

According to Wednesday's injury update from Max Bultman , Johansson will miss Thursday's game after suffering an injury during Detroit's 4-1 loss to the Calgary Flames on Saturday.

McLellan has not provided a timetable for the 25-year-old defenseman's return.

Johansson also missed Monday's 4-3 shootout victory over Edmonton, leaving Detroit without another regular contributor on the blue line.

The injury creates an additional challenge for McLellan, who has already been forced to make several lineup adjustments this season. William Wallinder and Andreas Englund are among the defensemen who could see additional opportunities while Johansson remains unavailable.

For now, the extent of Johansson's injury remains unclear.

Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton Still Weeks Away

The news wasn't particularly encouraging for Kasper or Appleton, either.

McLellan said both forwards are "probably two weeks away" from returning to action.

Kasper has been sidelined since early October with an upper-body injury, while Appleton has also been unavailable for several weeks because of an undisclosed injury.

As we previously reported , Kasper's absence created an immediate opening down the middle of Detroit's lineup and forced McLellan to experiment with Emmitt Finnie at center.

The Red Wings have continued adjusting their forward combinations, but getting both players healthy would provide some much-needed depth.

Their projected returns are not guaranteed, although McLellan's latest comments offer a clearer picture of when they might be available.

The Red Wings will now prepare for Thursday's matchup against Chicago without Johansson, Kasper, and Appleton.

With Detroit continuing to navigate several injury concerns , McLellan will need his available players to continue stepping up.

And while the injury report wasn't entirely encouraging, at least one mystery surrounding Wednesday's practice has been resolved.

articles.title: Fame Ijeboi is latest breakout RB for Purdue
articles.summary: Purdue sophomore Fame Ijeboi has emerged as a top Big Ten running back, fueling the team's explosive offense.
articles.body:
When you think of legendary Purdue running backs, a few come to mind. Kory Sheets. Markell Jones. Current Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. And very recently, Devin Mockobee, who has rejuvenate the position for a program that has needed some offensive minded inspiration of late. So it should have not surprise when a relatively unknown sophomore named Fame Ijeboi broke out this season. However, it was the unexpected nature of his development that has made Ijeboi one of the most pleasant surprises of the Big Ten season.

As it stands, in a conference predicated on the ground game, Ijeboi currently ranks sixth in total yards with 568. However, what's more impressive is that he is ranked second amongst all running backs with 9 total touchdowns. In fact, that number has him tied for third in the entire conference. Only Wayne Knight and Jeremiah Smith have more. Not such bad company for a player who many have probably never even heard of before this season.

What's been most important is that Purdue has actually been competitive as a result of his performance. A team that was expected to potentially finish last int the conference finds itself at 3-4 and 2-2 in Big Ten play. This is down to one of the most explosive offenses in the Big Ten. They average 409.1 yards per game and on the ground, 5.9 yards per carry.

Still, the offense seems to go as Ijeboi goes. If he's on his game, the aerial attack featuring the gutsy Ryan Browne at Qb and the reliable Asaad Waseem at receiver comes alive as well. In wins against Illinois and Minnesota, the offense combined for 65 points due to Ijeboi's strengths. However, when defenses bottle him up, like Washington did recently, the Purdue offense does seem to enter a lull.

For Penn State , it is imperative that they have come out of the bye having focused on shoring up their run defense. Ranking as one of the worst run defenses in the Big Ten, Penn State can ill afford for Ijeboi to have a good game. As evidenced by Northwestern, Penn State is capable of being gashed on the ground and if Purdue can exploit that, it may not be a good day at the office for Penn State.

articles.title: What's the series history between FSU and Clemson?
articles.summary: The series between the Clemson Tigers and the Florida State Seminoles is one of the more underrated ones in college football.
articles.body:
Florida State 's eighth game of the season is against the Clemson Tigers . The Seminoles and Tigers have one of the fiercest rivalries in the ACC, but what is the full series history between these two? Here's the full breakdown.

Florida State's record vs. Clemson is 21-17, as they meet every year. In their last appearance, the Seminoles lost to Clemson 24-10. In Clemson's last game against FSU, Cade Klubnik threw for 221 yards, one touchdown, and no interceptions. On the other hand, Tommy Castellanos went for 250 yards, one touchdown, and one pick.

Largest margin of victory: FSU 57, Clemson 0 (1993)

Smallest margin of victory: FSU 16, Clemson 13 (2010)

The Seminoles have a positive record against ACC teams since joining the conference in 1991 after being independent in football for 40 years. Per StatMuse , Florida State is 226-89-2 against the ACC. They average 31.7 points per game when facing an ACC team and have a strong record against many of their conference opponents.

In 2025, FSU would go on to finish 5-7 and would not make a bowl appearance. Clemson would play in the Pinstripe Bowl against Penn State, but would go on to lose, 22-10.

FSU will look to get its first win against Clemson at Doak since 2014 and move to 4-4 this season. Their match begins on Oct. 31, and fans can catch the game at 7 p.m. ET on the ACC Network.

articles.title: Security measures in place, blue line painted ahead of TCS NYC Marathon
articles.summary: Final preparations are underway for Sunday's TCS New York City Marathon, with crews painting the iconic blue line along the 26.2-mile course and setting up t...
articles.body:
Final preparations are underway for Sunday's TCS New York City Marathon, with crews painting the iconic blue line along the 26.2-mile course and setting up the finish line in Central Park.

The race marks the 50th running of the New York City Marathon and is expected to draw more than 60,000 runners and more than 2 million spectators.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the NYPD has been preparing for months alongside New York Road Runners and other agencies.

"This Sunday marks the 50th running of the NYC Marathon, one of the city's most celebrated traditions, bringing New Yorkers together and drawing visitors from around the world," Tisch said.

The race begins at 8 a.m. on the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, with waves of runners setting off throughout the morning before finishing in Central Park.

Tisch said there are currently no known specific or credible threats to this year's race, but New Yorkers can expect a heightened police presence along the route.

"New Yorkers will see an increased police presence, with thousands of NYPD officers posted along the entire route from Staten Island to the Bronx to right here in Central Park," she said.

Specialized units, including Emergency Service, Mounted, Canine, Harbor, Aviation and the Bomb Squad, will be deployed. Helicopters and drones will also be used to monitor the race in real time.

"There will be assets that you will see and others that you will not see," Tisch said.

Officials said hundreds of blocker vehicles and more than 10,000 metal barricades will be positioned along the route to protect runners and spectators. Intelligence teams will also monitor social media for potential threats, while response units will be ready to investigate reports citywide.

"Cops will be out there to keep you safe, but we ask everyone to stay alert. If you see something, please say something," Tisch said.

Spectators entering designated viewing areas in Central Park should be aware that bags are subject to inspection. Prohibited items include coolers, oversized bags, chairs, umbrellas and weapons. Officials also reminded the public that drones are prohibited.

Street closures will begin early Sunday, and drivers should expect rolling closures and delays near the route. Officials are encouraging people to use mass transit whenever possible.

The upper level of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge will close at 11 p.m. Saturday, followed by the lower level at 7 a.m. Sunday. The Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge, Pulaski Bridge, Willis Bridge and Madison Avenue Bridge will also close Sunday morning before reopening after runners clear those sections of the course.

The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon takes place on Sunday, November 1. Coverage on Channel 7 and wherever you stream ABC 7 New York begins with pre-race coverage, Marathon Sunday, at 7:00 a.m. Live coverage of Sunday's marathon begins at 8:00 a.m. only on Channel 7 and ESPN2.

articles.title: 6 storylines to watch in Jaguars vs. Colts in Week 8
articles.summary: Here are six storylines fans should watch in the Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Colts game in Week 8.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are taking on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8, fresh off a bye following back-to-back games in London.

On the surface, this looks like an easy game for the Jaguars to win. The Colts have been struggling this season, have issues at quarterback, and just traded away two of their best players. This game will also be played at home, where Jacksonville has a decade-long win streak over Indianapolis.

It would still be a mistake to underestimate the Colts, though. There will be a lot of motivation from Indianapolis to break their EverBank Stadium losing streak, and Jonathan Taylor is still one of the best running backs in the league. The Jaguars also have lost two games largely due to self-inflicted mistakes, so the issue may not even be losing to the Colts, but to themselves.

Which Colts quarterback will Jacksonville actually have to defend?

For now, Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen has said that Daniel Jones remains their starter at QB. Yet with Jones playing as poorly as he has been, and the Colts seemingly having thrown in the towel on their season, there has been plenty of talk of starting Anthony Richardson, who is currently QB2, or even Riley Leonard, who is QB3. Basically, given that the organization just traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Jacksonville needs to be ready for the possibility that Sunday's quarterback plan changes — either before the game or during it.

And if it does, the Jaguars defense will be looking at three very different styles of QB. Jones will come with the most conventional offense: pocket passing, some mobility, and Indy's normal structure. Richardson is notorious for being inaccurate, but he's also a monster athlete, so he would likely bring designed QB runs, read-option/RPO possibilities, scramble threat, and a huge arm. The defense will have to account for the quarterback as a legitimate runner on every snap. And Leonard, finally, is a much more mobile quarterback than Jones and could push Indy toward a simplified, movement-heavy offense, although without Richardson's freakish physical ceiling.

That creates a weird defensive-preparation challenge for Jacksonville. Richardson and Leonard both bring significantly more mobility than Jones, while Richardson in particular would fundamentally alter how the Jaguars have to defend the run game.

What do the Colts look like after abruptly beginning their tear-down?

It certainly appears that Indianapolis has thrown in the towel on the season, and trading away Nelson and Buckner is the biggest example. How will this affect the team? As Jaguars head coach Liam Coen explained today , feeling like there is nothing left to lose can make a team dangerous.

Still, it again makes it difficult for Jacksonville to prepare. What kind of team will be showing up on Sunday, and how will the Colts react to the losses of two of their best players?

Will Tyler Warren return, and how do the Jaguars handle him if he does?

Warren is a star tight end who missed Weeks 6 and 7 with a groin injury. Before that, he had become one of Indy's most reliable weapons , with 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns in five games, including 7-for-83 against Pittsburgh.

If he plays, Jacksonville has to deal with a very good young tight end who can become a security blanket for whichever quarterback is out there. If he doesn't, that's yet another important piece missing from an offense that's already struggling.

Can the Jaguars extend the 11-game home winning streak against the Colts?

Jacksonville has won every single home game against Indianapolis since 2015; the last time the Colts won at EverBank Stadium was on Sept. 21, 2014, when Andrew Luck threw for 370 yards and four touchdowns in a 44-17 Indianapolis win. The Jaguars have won every home game since, including one at Wembley Stadium in London that counted as a Jacksonville home game.

Last season, Jacksonville defeated Indianapolis 36-19 in Week 14, which gave them the lead in the AFC South for the rest of the season.

Can the Jaguars contain Jonathan Taylor behind a weakened offensive line?

There's no denying that Jacksonville has a monster run defense, but Taylor is also an elite running back who will always pose a threat. He is now even more obviously the centerpiece of that offense, and for now, Indy has no plans to trade him away.

However, with their Pro Bowler offensive lineman traded away, Taylor could have a difficult time. Will he still be able to turn in an elite performance, or will he be hampered by a combination of the Jaguars' run defense and a weakened offensive line?

Did the bye help Jacksonville solve the self-inflicted mistakes?

As mentioned, the Jaguars have lost two games that they arguably should have won, in part due to self-inflicted mistakes. This is especially true for the Week 2 loss to the Denver Broncos, in which Jacksonville led until falling apart in the second half. Penalties have been a major issue for this team so far this season.

Will the bye week have helped? Jacksonville has been good enough to overcome mistakes, but this week should be a game that the Jaguars win from start to finish. If penalties make this a close game again, it will signify a major problem.

articles.title: Royce Keys Talks WWE 2K26, 946, Carmelo Hayes, Bloodline, WarGames More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Royce Keys is taking WWE by storm as the leader of the 946 stable, and now a playable character in the WWE 2K26 video game.
articles.body:
Royce Keys is taking WWE by storm as the leader of the 946 stable, and now a playable character in the WWE 2K26 video game.

In a recent interview with Bleacher Report, Keys touched on several subjects, including being part of Ringside Pass Season 6, which is a DLC pack that makes him, Earthquake, Typhoon and Octagon Jr. usable in WWE 2K26.

Keys made his WWE debut as part of the men's Royal Rumble match back in January, and now he is a featured part of the product with his 946 group embroiled in a heated feud with The Bloodline.

Because of that, Keys' entry into WWE 2K26 comes at the perfect time, and it is something that is quite meaningful to the veteran Superstar.

"It's a great accomplishment because I think I've played almost every WWE video game, and I've always created myself," Keys said. "And now I don't have to do all the hard work of finding all the right moves, but it's definitely a very high accomplishment for me."

It turns out that Keys has been playing wrestling video games for much of his life, which makes being part of WWE 2K26 hit even closer to home for him.

"I got kids, so I play all the current stuff," Keys said. "In the past, I think one of my favorite ones that I was obsessed with as a kid was the Royal Rumble for Super Nintendo. And then another one was No Mercy. Then I got into the SmackDown vs. Raw games and the 2K. I even got some emulated games, the old WrestleFest game. I love them all."

WWE fans are undoubtedly itching for the chance to play as Keys in WWE 2K26 given how significant a part of WWE programming he has been in recent weeks and months.

On the Aug. 24 episode of Raw, Keys debuted the 946 stable with Bronco Nima and Lucien Price helping him attack The Usos, Solo Sikoa and LA Knight.

In the following weeks, Keys added Jaida Parker and Carmelo Hayes to the group, making them an even bigger threat to The Bloodline in the process.

Keys divulged that he was familiar with every member of 946 before bringing them into the stable, saying, "I knew everybody before we actually all got together. So, 946 is us. We've taken parts of how we grew up and where we're from and put them together, so it's something that's authentic and real."

He also stressed the importance of every member playing their part and contributing something unique, which is why Hayes and Parker were fitting choices to align with 946.

"We each bring something different," Keys said. "Melo's a little pit bull. When I take that leash off him, it's dangerous. And Jaida, she hits harder than some of the dudes. I always say it's like a pot of gumbo. You've got all these different flavors and mixtures in it, so it's gonna be hard for our opponents to adapt to it."

Hayes surprised the WWE Universe during the Oct. 12 edition of Raw when he joined 946 by attacking The Bloodline with a crowbar.

Just a couple of weeks before that, Parker became part of 946 when she shockingly hit Jacob Fatu with her vehicle, which was reminiscent of Rikishi doing the same to "Stone Cold" Steve Austin back in 1999.

Keys suggested that 946 accomplished its goal with the jaw-dropping stunt, saying, "It was shock value. Nothing has been seen like that since what? Stone Cold got hit by the car. Everything is calculated. All the i's are dotted and all the t's are crossed."

Because of that moment and others, such as lighting The Bloodline's vehicle on fire, many of the things 946 has done have been compared to segments that were commonplace during WWE's Attitude Era of the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Keys noted that although 946 isn't necessarily trying to bring back the Attitude Era, there has been a concerted effort to keep the audience guessing.

"There's never gonna be another Attitude Era," Keys said. "It doesn't make sense to recreate it. I just think that it's a whole new audience now, and you gotta keep everybody on their toes."

Whether the group is providing shocking moments backstage or wrestling in Raw main events, 946 has been one of the most heavily featured acts in WWE for quite some time, which speaks to how Keys and Co. are viewed by WWE officials.

"Those are prime-time spots," Keys said. "So, for us to be in those spots consistently, week after week, it means something. It's not by mistake."

Given where the 946 vs. The Bloodline rivalry is taking place on the WWE calendar, there has been a great deal of speculation among fans about the factions clashing in a WarGames match at Survivor Series on Nov. 28.

While Keys neither confirmed nor denied that a WarGames match is in the works, he made it clear that he and the rest of 946 have significant interest.

"It's something we would love to be a part of," Keys said. "If we are in it, just expect the unexpected, and just take what we've done now and multiply it by a hundred."

As for a potential World Heavyweight Championship match against Bloodline leader and Tribal Chief Roman Reigns coming out of Survivor Series, Keys said, "I'm after the grand prize. Nobody's safe."

Those who want a preview of a possible 946 vs. Bloodline WarGames match or Keys vs. Reigns singles match can make it happen with the WWE 2K26 Ringside Pass Season 6, which officially dropped Wednesday.
